544466|2026-09.headline: Aditya Infotech Q2 FY27 revenue rose 89.9% YoY to ₹1,746 crore, and FY27 revenue guidance was raised to ₹6,500–6,800 crore.
544466|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was ₹1,746 crore (+89.9% YoY, +24.5% QoQ) with EBITDA of ₹307 crore at a 17.6% margin, up from 14.8% in Q1. Reported PAT was ₹185.5 crore after a ₹34.4 crore exceptional fire loss at the Kadapa plant, which is insured; PAT before exceptional was ₹220 crore. Management raised FY27 revenue and PAT margin guidance but kept the EBITDA margin at 14–15%, citing expected lower second-half margins from input cost pressure in SOC and memory. The company completed a ₹1,500 crore QIP in September and became debt-free in October.

segments.name: CP Plus (core brand)
segments.commentary: About 88% of Q2 revenue vs 86% a year ago; IP products are about 79% of CP Plus, up from 71%. Company share of total Indian video surveillance market (incl. unorganised) was about 42% in the 12 months to Sep 2026, up from 30% at IPO.

segments.name: Nextiveo and Ira brands
segments.commentary: Nextiveo targets entry-level and Ira targets mid-market. Nextiveo's pickup is described as good; Ira's first products are expected to reach market by end-December 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue raised to ₹6,500–6,800 crore from ₹6,000–6,500 crore, implying 54–61% growth.
FY27 EBITDA margin kept at 14–15% despite 16.3% in H1, to keep a cushion for market share strategy and input cost volatility.
FY27 PAT margin raised to 9–10% from 8.5–9.5%.
Second-half margins expected to be below Q2 as low-cost SOC and memory inventory is used up and price increases are passed on gradually.
FY27 market share guided to 43–45%, up from the earlier view.
Backward integration benefits (housing, cable JV) expected mainly from FY28; not modelled into guidance yet.
Medium term: unit market growth of 18–20% over 3–5 years; value growth expected to exceed unit growth in the near term as prices still rise.
capex_capacity: Kadapa plant capacity is 2.5 million units per month; Kadapa phase 3 (22 acres newly acquired) and a new Greater Noida facility, funded from the QIP, aim to double capacity by FY29-early FY30.
Total capex planned at about ₹650 crore for the capacity doubling; Greater Noida civil construction starts next quarter, with capacity online in about 18–24 months.
Housing and enclosures plant in Kadapa begins trials this quarter, with commercial production next quarter; cable plant goes live in Q4 FY27.
Planned fully integrated lens plant in Greater Noida with capacity of 2 million lenses per month.
Blue K-Graph AI investment: ₹45.4 crore for 30% fully diluted stake, with one board seat and one observer seat; completion subject to customary conditions.
demand_pricing: Price increases on SOC, DDR and memory are being passed to channel gradually to protect market share and avoid a channel price shock; the company took strategic inventory positions ahead of cost increases.
About 40+ brands are STQC-certified per the online portal; management sees no significant on-ground entry traction yet.
Government policy on DVR/NVR is still a work in progress; no new notification issued as yet.

Channel reach: 30–35 thousand installers/resellers on the app and about 2,000 system integrators; management cites about 350,000 outlets in the addressable market, with the market leader present at 278,000.
Management said H1 growth of about 90% was partly helped by a soft base when STQC certification backlogs held back industry supply last year; H2 growth expected to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Given the 14–15% full-year margin guide, what do back-calculated H2 margins (~13%) imply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said backward integration benefits will mainly flow in FY28, and kept the 14–15% guide as a prudent cushion given volatile SOC and memory costs, as the company has historically over-delivered.

qa_highlights.question: What capabilities beyond Blue are being sought in inorganic moves?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a 'CP Plus 2.0' plan to move from hardware to solutions, cloud and AI with a global footprint. Targets are capabilities (AI, cloud, storage IP), product adjacencies and geographic expansion; specific targets were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is pricing being passed on gradually, and is there demand pushback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is staggering price increases to protect competitive position and grow share, aiming above the 43–45% share guide.

qa_highlights.question: Is Blue a meaningful revenue contributor over 3–5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Blue is mainly a technology and capability play, bringing cloud storage and analytics attach to cameras, not a standalone large revenue driver.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export plan and its timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export entry is planned within 18–24 months, focused on China-plus-one markets, with product mix (Pro or entry) varying by market; entry mode (own brand, partnership or OEM) is still being decided.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term growth and margin outlook beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 18–20% unit growth over 3–5 years; value growth should exceed unit growth near term as prices rise. Backward integration margin benefits are not yet modelled.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables improve and does it hold across brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tighter collection is a conscious effort and efficiency gain, and it expects similar receivable levels across Ira, Nextiveo and CP Plus Pro on a blended basis.

risks_watch: Input cost volatility in SOC, DDR and memory; the timing of price pass-through and the margin path in H2 FY27.
Working capital is elevated due to strategic inventory buys; receivable and inventory normalisation should be tracked.
Pending government policy on DVR/NVR certification could change domestic brand competition.
Ira brand launch (December 2026) and CP Plus Pro rollout (Q4 FY27) execution.
Capex execution: Greater Noida and Kadapa phase 3 (₹650 crore) timelines, and backward integration plants (housing, cables, lenses).
Full benefit of debt-free balance sheet and lower finance cost from H2 FY27.
Insurance claim on the Kadapa fire (₹34.4 crore exceptional item) settlement.
Blue K-Graph integration and the still-undisclosed CP Plus 2.0 acquisition pipeline.
544466|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on demand, share gains and the raised revenue and PAT guidance, but deliberately conservative on margins, with the EBITDA guide held at 14–15%. Management was evasive on specific M&A targets, the H1 growth split, and the housing plant spend, and deferred on backward integration benefits.
key_quotes: This has been the strongest half in our history.
Q2 should not be read as the run rate.
We want to be prudent and as our history is we have always over delivered from our guidance and we would want to maintain the cushion in order to ensure and go for market share as well.
The blue acquisition for us is more of a tech learning and less of a revenue or a bit of credit from an approach perspective.

544467|2026-03.headline: NSDL standalone PAT rose 5.2% YoY to INR79.7 crore in Q4 FY26; FY26 standalone PAT up 12.1% to INR360.6 crore despite weak capital markets.
544467|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the first full quarter cycle after the August 2025 listing, with standalone total income up 1.8% YoY to INR195.4 crore and EBITDA margin at 57.2%. Consolidated total income rose 23.6% YoY to INR486.8 crore, driven by subsidiaries, with consolidated PAT up 8.4% to INR90.3 crore. Management attributed the soft quarter to subdued capital market activity amid the West Asia conflict and FPI outflows. Net demat share held around 14% in Q4 versus 14.7% in Q3, with the decline attributed to episodic large-IPO and dormant-account closures by bank-based DPs. Management stressed continued technology and people investment, with a peak year expected in FY26-27 before plateauing.

financial_highlights.change: +5.2% YoY from INR75.8 crore; PAT margin 40.8%
+12.1% YoY from INR321 crore; PAT margin 43.2%
+13.9% YoY; recurring revenue about 50% of total
+8.4% YoY from INR83.3 crore; PAT margin 18.6%
+10.8% YoY from INR343 crore; PAT margin 22.9%

segments.name: Depository (standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone Q4 PAT INR79.7 crore and FY26 PAT INR360.6 crore; standalone share of consolidated profit fell to about 90% from 95% as subsidiaries grew.

segments.name: NSDL Payments Bank
segments.commentary: Deposit balances crossed INR500 crore (about INR521 crore) with 43.5 lakh customers; CASA float above INR500 crore; ranked 7th as payee PSP app; UPI acquiring volumes up 6x YoY. Management said Q3-to-Q4 revenue jump reflected high gross throughput in transaction banking, not restatement.

segments.name: NSDL Database Management (NDML)
segments.commentary: Added about 33.5 lakh insurance policies in FY26; insurance top line about INR5.5-6 crore. SEZ pricing revised in February 2026. Insurance repository business being demerged into a new company per IRDAI directions.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 technology capex broadly similar to FY26, with opex possibly marginally higher; FY26 and FY27 together described as the peak investment period, with capex declining thereafter.
Manpower additions expected to be much lower in FY27 than FY26, with productivity and employee-band tightening starting in April 2026.
Management expects one more year of elevated technology and people costs, then plateauing.
Custody fee direction described as difficult to predict; management cited secular growth trend tied to account sourcing.
No update on the regulatory case for an increase in annual issuer fee; discussions with regulator are bilateral.
capex_capacity: FY26 capitalisation of INR106.1 crore, with technology spend of INR91.4 crore; split between infrastructure resilience/capacity, DP integration licences and cybersecurity including DC-DR air gap per SEBI circular.
Capitalised intangibles roughly doubled YoY per analyst question; attributed to licences, applications and cybersecurity spend.
More than 40 APIs launched, with API interoperability expanded to clearing corporations and bond platforms during the quarter.
Demat accounts at NSDL reached 4.44 crore; 311 DPs, with 21 DPs added in FY26 (a record).
demand_pricing: FY26 net demat account additions of 49.4 lakh versus 36.8 lakh in FY25; incremental market share 15.4% for FY26.

Q4 FY26 incremental net demat share about 14%, versus 9.6% in Q4 FY25 and 14.7% in Q3 FY26; decline attributed to a large IPO benefiting competitors and bank-based DPs closing dormant accounts at year end.
Management says gross market share is holding; net share decline described as episodic.
Yuva plan contributes 21% of incremental demat sourcing; women's demat plan with 3-year settlement fee waiver launched April 1, 2026.
Fintech DP wins: one DP moved from competition to NSDL with about 70,000 accounts last year rising to 700,000 this year (10x).
Margin pledge income steady, growing about 5-7% in transaction count; MTF book growth is in value terms, not transactions.
Corporate action and IPO income fell to about INR16 crore in FY26 from INR34 crore in the prior-year period, due to bonus and rights issues last year.
Custody: unlisted company accounts moderated after definition change; exit folio up about 15% to about 14 crore folios.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for annual custody fee growth, folio reset and issuer fee case with regulator?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said custody growth is secular and tied to account sourcing; the unlisted-company slowdown and a definition change moderated growth. Regulator discussions are bilateral and nothing has happened yet on the issuer fee.

qa_highlights.question: Is incremental account addition coming from new DPs or the banking channel, and how much of the market is still untapped?
qa_highlights.answer: DP segment scaled 10x to 700,000 accounts from 70,000; a Pune-based fintech moved fully to NSDL; several large DPs will contribute only from FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Where are we in the technology and people investment journey?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 was the peak; FY27 tech capex broadly similar with slight opex rise; capex to decline after that. Manpower additions much lower; employee band tightening started April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp QoQ jump in banking revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited quality account sourcing, CASA float above INR500 crore, transaction charges of INR43 lakh, and UPI acquiring fees; Jigar Shah said no restatement, with high gross throughput in transaction banking.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the margin pledge income flat while the MTF book grew about 68-70%?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin pledge is a steady business growing about 5-7% by transaction count; the MTF growth is in value terms because ticket sizes rose, and NSDL revenue is transaction-based.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall from INR117 crore to about INR100 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the prior year included a regulatory settlement charge; underlying costs are stable with no cost reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue foregone on Yuva accounts and NDML/payments bank growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not quantify Yuva revenue foregone; Yuva customers were a small share of settlement contribution. On subsidiaries, management declined to forecast, citing regulatory interventions; NDML has four revenue lines and subsidiary profit contribution moved to 90:10 from 95:5.

risks_watch: Net market share on a net basis declined QoQ in Q4 (14% vs 14.7%); monitor whether episodic factors reverse in Q1 FY27.
Custody fee growth slowed in the last two quarters; the Q1 folio reset and unlisted-company definition change are open questions.
Regulatory risk on payments bank (repeated interventions) and NDML (charge reduction mandated last year; KYC pricing change; insurance repository demerger).
Elevated technology and people costs continue for one more year before plateauing.
Weak capital markets: FPI outflows, geopolitical conflict, and lower demat account additions industry-wide (3.2 crore FY26 vs 4.1 crore FY25).

rows.why: Several large DPs will contribute only from FY27, and one fintech DP grew from 70,000 to 700,000 accounts (10x), which supports account additions.

rows.why: Manpower additions are guided much lower in FY27 than FY26 and employee-band tightening started in April 2026, which can ease people cost growth after one more year of elevated spend.

544467|2026-06.headline: NSDL Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 7.9% YoY to INR89.1 crores, with EBITDA margin at 57.8% amid front-loaded tech and manpower spend.
544467|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income grew 15.3% YoY to INR219.7 crores and PAT rose 7.9% to INR89.1 crores, while management flagged margin moderation from front-loaded technology and hiring. Consolidated total income rose 61.6% YoY to INR560.5 crores, but consolidated PAT grew a slower 9.7% to INR98.3 crores, with the payments bank's one-time onboarding revenue carrying low margins. Demat additions improved: NSDL's incremental market share in net demat account additions rose to 17.6% from about 15.5% a year earlier, with 12.4 lakh net additions. Management stressed that YoY comparison is more meaningful than QoQ given seasonality in e-voting and subsidiary dividends.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR106 crores for full FY26

segments.name: Depository (standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone revenue INR182.2 crores (+13.2% YoY); standalone profit is about 91% of consolidated profit. Demat accounts on NSDL reached 4.56 crores, with 12.4 lakh net additions versus 10.4 lakh a year earlier.

segments.name: NSDL Payments Bank (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Drove consolidated revenue growth but margins were diluted by upfront onboarding revenue sharing with a partner on a specific card-led project. Retail customers rose 1.7x YoY to 49.5 lakh from 28.3 lakh; ranked 6th as payee PSP among top 15 banks as of June 30, 2026.

segments.name: NSDL Database Management (NDML)
segments.commentary: Includes KRA, SEZ online and insurance repository businesses. KRA income fell about 2% YoY despite a 20% cut in KYC fetch charges, offset by SEZ growth. Insurance repository business is being moved into a separate subsidiary per IRDAI guidance.

Board approved investment in IIBH, a GIFT City associate in which NSDL holds 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Are employee costs (up about 40% on standalone) near peak run-rate, and where is headcount being added?
qa_highlights.answer: Jigar Shah said most FY26 hiring (net about 98 employees in the prior year) is now flowing through costs; hiring will be 'very cautious' from here, with recent recruits' costs hitting coming quarters. Adds were mainly in technology and cybersecurity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the payments bank arrangement behind the revenue jump, and is the current run-rate sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Vijay Chandok said it is a specific card-related project where onboarding joining fees are largely passed through to a partner, so margins are low. Onboarding peaked in Q1 and Q2 should normalise toward Q4 levels; he explicitly said this is not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the tech spend regulator-driven or market-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Chandok split spend into four areas: resilience (regulatory and market overlap, a sizable area), customer experience (mainly market-driven), automation/AI/ML (internal), and infrastructure refresh on a 5-7 to 8 year cycle.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the annual custody fee growth and folio count?
qa_highlights.answer: Jigar Shah said about 33,000 companies were onboarded in FY25 and 30,000 in FY26; folio count is about 14 crore versus 11.9 crore a year earlier. Market share in unlisted companies is about 70%+.

qa_highlights.question: What drove pledge income growth and KYC income resilience at NDML?
qa_highlights.answer: Shah attributed pledge growth to MTF book activity and pledge/unpledge counts up about 15% YoY. Chandok said the 20% KRA fetch-charge cut was partly offset by SEZ growth, and NDML subsidiary split would not be shared yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the fintech share of new accounts jumped from about 2% to about 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Chandok said work over the last several quarters (customer meetings, back-office vendor workshops, features, relationship building) led to about 4-month onboarding per fintech; ramp-ups are gradual and accelerating, with more fintechs now in the journey.

qa_highlights.question: What were the major hits and misses since the CEO joined and what are next-year priorities?
qa_highlights.answer: Chandok cited four themes: technology modernisation (largely done at basic level), skills/leadership gap (largely complete), market penetration (good progress), and IPO completed in 7 months. Next focus is residual tech modernisation, automation, resilience and customer experience.

qa_highlights.question: Are DPs onboarded in the last year converting to demat accounts, and what is the DP ramp timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Chandok said DP onboarding takes about 12-16 weeks; the 21 DPs added in FY26 are exclusively on NSDL, so accounts flow to NSDL once live, and many are in integration or early scale-up. Expected benefit is contingent on market conditions.

rows.why: Management said onboarding peaked in Q1 and Q2 should normalise toward Q4 levels, but explicitly said this is not guidance; consolidated revenue of INR516.6 crore (+65.6% YoY) was inflated by low-margin onboarding.

tone.note: Management was confident on market share (17.6% incremental), account additions and the DP pipeline, but cautious and non-committal on the payments bank run-rate, forward margins and subsidiary-level details; analysts pressed on employee cost run-rate, payments bank sustainability and KRA pressure.

544467|2026-09.headline: NSDL Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34.8% YoY to INR582.6 crores, but PAT grew only 10.9% to INR122.5 crores on elevated tech and talent costs.
544467|2026-09.overview: Consolidated total income reached INR582.6 crores (+34.8% YoY), driven by a rebound in IPO and corporate-action activity, while PAT rose 10.9% YoY to INR122.5 crores. Consolidated EBITDA grew 12.5% YoY to INR178.5 crores, with margin at 30.6%, as technology and talent spending stayed elevated. Management said FY27 technology and related expenses would be broadly flat versus FY26, with growth moderating from next year, and gave no price-hike progress on issuer or settlement charges. Demat account additions were 15.6 lakh net in Q2, and NSDL's market share was 17.2% in Q2 versus 17.6% QoQ.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR106.1 crores in full FY26

segments.name: Depository (standalone core)
segments.commentary: Standalone PAT is about 88% of consolidated profit. Demat accounts reached 4.72 crore, with 320 DPs after adding about 4 in Q2 and 10 in H1. Market share was 17.2% in Q2 versus 17.6% QoQ, and 17.4% in H1 versus 16.6% in H1 FY26.

segments.name: NSDL Payments Bank
segments.commentary: Retail customers rose to 54.3 lakh from 33.5 lakh a year earlier (1.6x). Deposits grew 1.4x to INR378.1 crores. Subsidiary profit contribution is said to be above 10%, up from about 5% a year or 1.5 years earlier. Management cited UPI acquiring tie-ups as a growth driver.

segments.name: NSDL Database Management (KRA and insurance repository)
segments.commentary: KRA records reached 2.06 crore as of 30 September 2026. Cumulative dematerialised insurance policies were 1.75 crore. The insurance repository business is being transferred via a demerger application filed with NCLT Mumbai.

guidance_outlook: FY27 technology and related expenses are expected to be broadly flat versus FY26, with marginal differences possible; a specific action plan for next year is due in the next few months.
Management expects the base effect to flatten expense growth from next year, but gave no time frame for operating leverage or margin normalisation.
No guidance on market share or account additions; management said it was not giving specific guidance on retail share gains.
Settlement and issuer pricing talks with regulators remain unresolved for more than a year; no price-hike outcome to report.
capex_capacity: Technology capex rose from about INR30 crores to more than INR100 crores; spending has since flattened, per management.
Capitalised technology was INR23.9 crores in H1 FY27 versus INR106.1 crores in full FY26.
Demat 2.0 (DLT-based, tokenised bonds, CBDC settlement) is in SEBI sandbox pilot, jointly run with CDSL; 3 primary bond issuances worth a little over INR1,000 crores so far, institutional only.
Online Form 121 submission, an API-based interface with NSE for Electronic Gold Receipts, and API connectivity for bond OBPPs went live; 68+ APIs are offered to DPs.
demand_pricing: Q2 FY27 net demat additions were 15.6 lakh, against 79 lakh industry-wide additions in Q2 FY26 (about 90 lakh in Q2 FY27 industry-wide, up 14.2% YoY).
Fintech brokers were 23.5% of NSDL's incremental demat sourcing in Q2 FY27, up from 9.3% in Q2 FY26.
Run-rate market share on new accounts was about 9%, then 12%, then 14%, and is now 16-18% per management.
Unlisted issuer segment share was about 72.5%, with 3,197 companies admitted in Q2; e-voting share was about 52.4%, with 3,160 events versus 2,924 a year earlier.
IPO activity: about INR90,000 crore raised in Q2 FY27 across the primary market, including the NSE listing. Management said IPOs add roughly 25-30% to business when the pipeline is strong.
Unlisted company onboarding was about 6,500 in H1 FY27 versus about 30,000 in FY26 and 33,000 before that; management described this as saturation.
Issuer and settlement charges were unchanged; there was no IPO price increase.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the Demat 2.0 opportunity, what stage is it at, and is NSDL a first mover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described it as a SEBI-driven sandbox pilot run jointly with CDSL, with bond issuance only and no secondary market yet. Three issuances worth a little over INR1,000 crore have happened, and it is open only to institutions. Retail access depends on future SEBI evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for raising retail market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called retail share gain the top priority and said the top 3 DPs hold about 60-65% of the market. About 30 new DPs were added in 1.5 years, and run-rate share has climbed from 9% to 16-18%. No specific guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will IPO and corporate action momentum continue?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Jigar Shah said YoY growth was about 24%. IPO activity adds roughly 25-30% to business when the pipeline is strong, and October saw one large IPO. Continued momentum depends on SEBI approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Will unlisted company onboarding keep falling, and how are tech expenses expected to trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said onboarding has stabilised at about 3,000 per quarter after the MCA dematerialisation rule change. Tech spend in FY27 is expected to be broadly flat versus FY26, moving from catch-up to build-up mode, with a specific action plan for next year due in coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a case for an issuer pricing hike given rising costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no IPO price increase. Settlement-charge talks with regulators have been ongoing for over a year, with no outcome yet.

qa_highlights.question: Will negative operating leverage persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit to a time frame, citing base effects and market dependence. It said FY27 spend is largely budgeted, with future spend more discretionary, and that normalisation must come before operating leverage returns.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Payments Bank traction and MDR outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers are at 54 lakh, deposits at INR378 crore, and UPI acquiring tie-ups are growing. The MDR on UPI is paused, and its impact on the Payments Bank has not been quantified.

risks_watch: Consolidated PAT growth (10.9%) lags revenue growth (34.8%), so cost growth on technology, talent and depreciation is outpacing income.
Retail market share remains about 17%, and the top 3 DPs control about 60-65% of the market.
Unlisted company onboarding is saturating, which reduces a recurring revenue stream.
Issuer and settlement charge pricing is unresolved, with no timeline for regulatory action.
Dependence on IPO and corporate-action cycles; management says IPOs add 25-30% when the pipeline is strong.
Payments Bank profitability depends on UPI acquiring and on MDR regulation, which is currently paused.
544467|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on franchise growth, Demat 2.0 and Payments Bank traction, but cautious and non-committal on costs and pricing. Management repeatedly declined to give guidance on expense normalisation, market share and timing of operating leverage.
key_quotes: So one has to look at technology investments as a medium-term business enabler really rather than just an expense, and that's how we see it.
There are no progress or I would say, outcomes to report as far as price increases are concerned.
So it is not as if we are, in a sense, got early mover, but we have moved together.
Before negative operating leverage starts kicking in, you need to show normalization of expenses and then operating leverage comes in.

rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 30.6% and EBITDA up only 12.5% vs total income up 34.8%, but management gave no timeframe and said FY27 tech spend is broadly flat vs FY26, so operating leverage depends on expense flattening from next year and market activity.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity or plant expansion discussed; tech capitalisation fell to INR23.9 crores in H1 FY27 from INR106.1 crores in full FY26 and spend has flattened, so no new capacity is signalled.

rows.why: Net demat additions were 15.6 lakh in Q2 vs 79 lakh industry-wide in Q2 FY26, NSDL's share slipped to 17.2% from 17.6% QoQ, and IPO activity (about INR90,000 crore raised in Q2) adds 25-30% to business when the pipeline is strong, but the unlisted onboarding base is saturating at about 3,000 per quarter.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Technology capex has flattened after rising from about INR30 crores to over INR100 crores, and utilisation is not a relevant metric for this depository; no new capex was announced.

rows.why: PAT growth of 10.9% lags income growth of 34.8%, FY27 tech spend is budgeted flat, and issuer and settlement price-hike talks are unresolved for over a year, leaving no pricing cushion if IPO activity slows.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Demat 2.0 (DLT-based tokenised bonds and CBDC settlement) is in a SEBI sandbox with 3 bond issuances worth a little over INR1,000 crores, institutional only, and retail access depends on future SEBI evaluation; not yet commercial.

rows.label: Payments Bank UPI acquiring and customer growth
rows.why: Retail customers reached 54.3 lakh (1.6x YoY) and deposits INR378.1 crores (1.4x), with the subsidiary's profit contribution above 10% and UPI acquiring tie-ups cited as the growth driver, though MDR is paused and its impact is unquantified.

rows.label: Insurance repository demerger to NCLT
rows.why: A demerger application for the insurance repository business has been filed with NCLT Mumbai, with 1.75 crore cumulative dematerialised policies, but no approval timeline was given.

rows.label: Issuer and settlement charge hike
rows.why: Settlement and issuer pricing talks with regulators have been unresolved for more than a year, with no IPO price increase and no timeline for regulatory action.

tone.note: Management was confident on the franchise, Demat 2.0 and Payments Bank traction, but cautious and non-committal on tech and talent costs, pricing and operating leverage timing; analysts pressed on margin normalisation, market share and the IPO cycle.

544469|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 pre-sales rose 177% YoY to INR462 crores, but collections were only INR82 crores against INR308 crores revenue.
544469|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 pre-sales of INR462 crores (up 177% YoY), revenue of INR308 crores (up 62% YoY) and PAT of INR101 crores (up 17% YoY). FY26 pre-sales were INR1,157 crores (up 137%), revenue INR769 crores (up 40%) and PAT INR243 crores. Collections remained weak at INR82 crores in Q4 and INR376 crores for FY26, which management attributed to all four newly launched projects being in basement stage. Management guided FY27 pre-sales of INR1,800-2,000 crores with revenue and PAT growth of 55-60%, and a launch pipeline of six projects worth INR5,000-5,500 crores GDV.

segments.name: Residential (ultra-luxury, Mumbai)
segments.commentary: Lotus Celestia (Versova) booked INR155 crores within 7 days of March 2026 launch, GDV INR1,400-1,500 crores. Amalfi sold about 61-62% and The Arcadian 41%, Varun 38% within a year of launch.

segments.name: Commercial
segments.commentary: Two new commercial projects in Andheri West to launch in H1 FY27 (Lotus Sky Plaza and Lotus Trident); management expects 10-20% pricing premium to rivals.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales guidance INR1,800-2,000 crores, revenue growth 55-60% and PAT growth 55-60%.
Six planned launches (Aquaria, Trident, Aurelia, Sky Plaza, Portofino, Odyssey) with GDV INR5,000-5,500 crores; three launches in H1 FY27 with combined revenue potential INR2,500-3,000 crores.
Project cost inflation estimated at about 1% annualised; management also cited a 1.5-2.5% range for total project cost.
Margins expected to remain in the guided range despite marketing spend below 1% of revenue.
Collections expected to improve in Q1 and H1 FY27 as projects move from basement to plinth and superstructure.
Target to sign four to six new projects in the coming year.
Dividend payout of 50% for FY26 approved; promoter group waived its FY26 dividend. Company is formulating a dividend policy.
capex_capacity: Aquaria (Prabhadevi): 100% approvals, work started, launch planned this quarter.
Trident: full approvals, launch planned this quarter.
Sky Plaza (Andheri): about 80% approvals obtained, H1 FY27 launch.
Remaining three H2 launches expected to get all approvals in Q1 FY27 with launch the following quarter.
Lotus Monarch, Lotus Avalon and Lotus Solana delayed; one project needs a separate hospital to be built before sale area is separated.
Net IPO proceeds of about INR732 crores (fresh issue INR792 crores gross); INR394 crores deployed till March 2026.
Projected free cash flow: INR3,103 crores from completed and ongoing projects, INR5,450 crores from upcoming, total INR8,553 crores.
demand_pricing: Management says ultra-luxury (INR10-12 crore+ tickets) demand is strong and insulated from external forces; pricing about 10-20% (up to 25%) above competitors in each micro market.
Nine new projects added in FY26 with cumulative GDV of about INR8,500-9,000 crores.
Q4 pre-sales INR462 crores include INR203 crores from Varun, Arcadian and Amalfi, and INR358 crores from FY26 launches.
Arc One realisations rose after occupation certificate and amenity completion, per management.
Marketing campaign 'Luxury Coastline Collection' covers 11 projects across Versova, Juhu, Carter Road, Bandstand, Prabhadevi and Nepean Sea Road.

qa_highlights.question: Collections are low versus revenue despite milestone-linked billing; when will they pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said collections are low because all four new projects are in basement stage, where expenses are high but customer dues are small; collections are expected to improve in Q1 FY27 and H1 as projects reach plinth and slabs.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence in INR1,800-2,000 crore FY27 pre-sales amid slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ultra-luxury demand is strong and that the four existing projects plus six new launches would together deliver about INR1,800 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue recognised from FY26 pre-sales?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said INR460 crores of revenue was recognised from the INR1,157 crores of FY26 pre-sales, which he described as the Q4 figure.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Monarch, Avalon and Solana delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two projects need multiple approvals, including construction of an existing hospital to separate the sale area.

qa_highlights.question: Cost pressure from geopolitical tensions?
qa_highlights.answer: Input costs rose about 7% and labour about 5%; management estimated total project cost impact at 2-2.5%, with no import component in supply chain.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a dividend policy is being formulated for deliberation at the next board meeting; 50% payout declared for non-promoter shareholders for FY26.

risks_watch: Collections (INR82 crores in Q4 vs INR308 crores revenue) lag recognition; FY26 collections of INR376 crores versus INR769 crores revenue. Watch Q1 FY27 collections as the four new projects reach plinth.
FY27 guidance depends on six launches (INR5,000-5,500 crores GDV) and on approvals for Sky Plaza (about 80%) and the H2 projects; Monarch, Avalon and Solana are already delayed.
Management's cost-inflation figures vary across the call (about 1% annualised versus 1.5-2.5% total project cost), so the margin impact is not clearly quantified.
Ghatkopar matter (about INR600 crores GDV) is pending at the Supreme Court; outcome expected this year.
Q4 PAT growth of 17% was well below the 62% revenue growth; the drivers were not explained on the call.
Management said the dividend policy is still being formulated.
544469|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on demand and FY27 targets, with strong statements on ultra-luxury pricing power. Evasive on collections, approval delays and the Ghatkopar matter, and gave limited numerical detail on cost and margin impact.
key_quotes: So we are very confident that we will be able to achieve that.
Fortunately, we do not have any import component in our supply chain.
Pre-sales for Q4 FY26 stood at INR462 crores, registering a strong growth of 177% year-on-year.

rows.why: Management says margins stay in the guided range, but Q4 EBITDA margin was 39.4% and FY26 was 36.5%, while input costs rose about 7% and labour about 5%, with project cost inflation estimated at about 1% annualised (1.5-2.5% total project cost), so the margin direction is not clearly quantified and no expansion was guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Three new launches are planned in H1 FY27 (Aquaria and Trident this quarter, Sky Plaza in H1 with about 80% approvals), with three more H2 launches expected to get approvals in Q1 FY27, but Monarch, Avalon and Solana are delayed and the Ghatkopar matter is pending, so timing carries risk.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 pre-sales guided at INR1,800-2,000 crores versus INR1,157 crores in FY26 (about 55-73% growth), and revenue growth of 55-60% is guided, backed by six launches worth INR5,000-5,500 crores GDV, though collections of INR82 crores in Q4 against INR308 crores revenue show execution still lags.

rows.why: Management guided FY27 pre-sales of INR1,800-2,000 crores and revenue and PAT growth of 55-60%, with no sign of running ahead of this; Q4 PAT grew only 17% against 62% revenue growth, so there is no evidence yet of an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Monarch, Avalon and Solana are delayed, Sky Plaza is only about 80% approved, and collections (INR82 crores in Q4, INR376 crores in FY26 against INR769 crores revenue) lag, so FY27 pre-sales of INR1,800-2,000 crores depend on launches that are not yet fully approved.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Six named launches (Aquaria, Trident, Aurelia, Sky Plaza, Portofino, Odyssey) with GDV INR5,000-5,500 crores, three of them in H1 FY27 with combined revenue potential of INR2,500-3,000 crores, and Aquaria and Trident already at approval stage with launches planned this quarter.

rows.label: Collections catch-up as new projects reach plinth
rows.why: Collections were INR82 crores in Q4 against INR308 crores revenue and INR376 crores for FY26 against INR769 crores, with management expecting improvement as the four new projects move from basement to plinth and superstructure.

rows.label: Ultra-luxury pricing premium of 10-20% (up to 25%)
rows.why: Management says pricing is 10-20% (up to 25%) above competitors in each micro market, with Lotus Celestia booking INR155 crores within 7 days of launch and Q4 pre-sales of INR462 crores.

rows.label: Ghatkopar matter at Supreme Court (about INR600 crores GDV)
rows.why: The matter is pending at the Supreme Court with an outcome expected this year, and it covers about INR600 crores of GDV that could be affected either way.

tone.note: Management was confident on ultra-luxury demand, pricing power and the INR1,800-2,000 crore FY27 pre-sales target, but was evasive on weak collections, approval delays for Monarch, Avalon and Solana, and the Ghatkopar matter, and gave little numerical detail on cost and margin impact.

544469|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 pre-sales rose 567% YoY to INR409 crores and PAT grew 77% to INR46 crores at a 34.5% margin.
544469|2026-06.overview: Sri Lotus reported strong Q1 FY27 growth: pre-sales INR409 crores, collections INR150 crores (+115% YoY), revenue INR132 crores (+116%), and EBITDA INR48 crores (36.4% margin). Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR1,800-2,000 crores pre-sales and 55-60% revenue and PAT growth. A new Juhu commercial redevelopment (GDV about INR1,600 crores) was won, and the company reported a net cash balance sheet of INR623 crores. Q&A surfaced some inconsistencies on launch timing and the split of Q1 pre-sales between new and existing launches.

segments.name: Residential redevelopment (Mumbai ultra-luxury)
segments.commentary: Core focus; 17 of 22 pipeline projects are redevelopment-led. Management says micro-market pricing is 10-15% above other developers, with 5-10% price rises seen over the past year.

segments.name: Commercial
segments.commentary: Two commercial projects in the pipeline; Juhu commercial-cum-retail redevelopment (GDV about INR1,600 crores) won, expected to start next year after approvals and take 3-4 years to complete.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales guidance maintained at INR1,800-2,000 crores; management said it will 'easily achieve' INR1,800 crores.
FY27 revenue and PAT growth guidance of 55-60% maintained.
EBITDA margin guidance 35-40% and PAT margin 25-30% stated in the prepared remarks; in Q&A the CEO quoted EBITDA margin of 33-36%, a discrepancy.
FY27 cash collections target of about INR1,000 crores, supported by billing on Arcadian and Varun (each about 90% complete) and Amalfi (60-70%) by year-end.

Four further launches in FY27 with combined GDV of INR3,500-4,000 crores: Lotus Sky Plaza (Oshiwara, about INR1,500 crores, H1-end or early Q3), Lotus Odyssey (Bandstand, about INR1,000 crores, Q4), Lotus Portofino (Versova, about INR500 crores, within 3-4 months), Lotus Aurelia (Napean Sea Road, INR600-700 crores).
Gift City project: mixed-use approvals (commercial, retail, residential) expected by end-2026, with construction to start after approvals.
Promoter stake about 82%; management targets dilution to 75% or below within the remaining two years of a three-year window, with no investor discussions yet.
capex_capacity: Two projects launched in Q1 FY27: Lotus Trident (Andheri West) and Lotus Aquaria (Prabhadevi), together GDV of INR1,350 crores; Aquaria company GDV about INR800 crores (saleable, excluding tenant areas), starting price about INR85,000 per sq ft.
Varun: plinth just completed, about 20 slabs; RCC work targeted by January and 90% of work by March.
Arcadian and Varun targeted at 90% of project cost and Amalfi at 60-70% by end-FY27.

Juhu commercial redevelopment: plot over 5,000 sq m; start next year after plan approvals, 3-4 years to complete. Part of the area to be rehoused for existing tenants, remainder for commercial pipeline; no rental retention decided.
Of the INR550 crores earmarked for subsidiary projects (Amalfi, Arcadian, Varun), INR271 crores deployed as of 30 June 2026. Net IPO proceeds about INR732 crores after INR792 crores fresh issue.
demand_pricing: Q1 pre-sales of INR409 crores: management said only about INR25 crores came from the two new launches; the remainder came from projects launched in FY26 and earlier. Trident already reported about INR150 crores of sales within one month, in July-August.
Management said about INR400-plus crores of sales came from Trident, Aquaria and Celestia over the last two quarters.
Sales pace: 20-30% of inventory sold at launch, then about 30% of stock offloaded per year over a roughly three-year build cycle.
Brand campaign across 11 Mumbai coastal projects is ongoing; sales and marketing spend about 1% of pre-sales, which management expects to be offset by lower brokerage.
Management cited Mumbai luxury housing demand growth of more than 11% while the broader market moderated; constrained supply in Worli, Bandra and South Mumbai.
Versova: three existing sea-facing projects with more society talks under way.

qa_highlights.question: Can the INR409 crore pre-sales support the INR2,000 crore FY27 guidance, and what supports 55-60% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO Sanjay Jain said the company is confident of easily achieving the INR1,800 crore pre-sales guidance, citing four new launches and strong response to Trident, Aquaria and Celestia.

qa_highlights.question: Timing and GDV of the upcoming launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Lotus Sky Plaza (Oshiwara, about INR1,500 crores) at H1-end or start of Q3; Lotus Odyssey (Bandstand, about INR1,000 crores) in Q4; Lotus Portofino (Versova, about INR500 crores) within 3-4 months; Lotus Aurelia (Napean Sea Road, INR600-700 crores).

qa_highlights.question: Juhu project details, margin and rental plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is more than 5,000 sq m plot in middle Juhu with existing shops and offices to be rehoused; no rental retention for this project. EBITDA around 40% and PAT 25-30% expected, which management said it will achieve or beat.

qa_highlights.question: Gap between Q1 pre-sales split and launch-driven sales?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Rakesh Gupta said about INR25 crores came from the two new launches, with the balance from FY26 and earlier launches. The CEO had earlier cited Trident's INR150 crores within one month, which relates to July-August rather than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Cash collection goal and EBITDA margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Collection target about INR1,000 crores this year as billing rises on Arcadian, Varun and Amalfi. CEO said EBITDA margin is in the 33-36% range, which differs from the 35-40% guidance in the prepared remarks.

qa_highlights.question: Price increases and premium versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Price rises of 5-10% over the past year. Pricing about 10-15% above other developers in the same micro-markets, per the CEO.

qa_highlights.question: Leverage plans and net worth?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment is about 10% of GDV in redevelopment. Management cited total GDV of about INR18,000 crores and net worth of about INR1,900 crores, with annual net worth additions expected.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter stake dilution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter stake about 82%; management said there are three years to reach 75% or below, with two years remaining, but no investor discussions yet.

rows.why: Juhu redevelopment (GDV about INR1,600 crore) is won and starts after approvals next year, and Gift City approvals are targeted by end-2026, but no new capex quantum is stated and investment is about 10% of GDV in redevelopment.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Four launches are guided (Sky Plaza, Odyssey, Portofino, Aurelia) with combined GDV of INR3,500-4,000 crore, though launch timing is inconsistent across answers.

rows.label: Juhu commercial redevelopment won (GDV about INR1,600 crore)

544469|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 pre-sales rose 83% YoY to INR470 crore and EBITDA more than doubled to INR107 crore at a 39.9% margin.
544469|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong Q2 and H1 FY27 growth in pre-sales, revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with margins above 38%. Three redevelopment projects were added in the quarter, adding an estimated INR2,700-2,800 crore GDV, taking the pipeline to 24 projects and about INR20,000 crore GDV. Collections were weaker at INR60 crore in Q2 and INR209 crore in H1, which management attributed to construction-linked billing and expects to improve in H2. Analysts focused on collections, the INR300 crore business development outflow, Prabhadevi sales traction and project timeline slippage.

segments.name: Lotus Trident (Andheri West, luxury commercial)
segments.commentary: Contributed INR178 crore pre-sales in its first full quarter after end-June launch, about 35% of sales sold within three months per management. Management guided EBITDA margin of 33-35%.

segments.name: Residential luxury projects
segments.commentary: Celestia reported 36% sales within six months of launch. Lotus Aquaria (Prabhadevi) reported healthy inquiries, but Lotus Prabhadevi (GDV ~INR800 crore) contributed no pre-sales in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales guidance reiterated at INR1,800-2,000 crore.
FY27 revenue and PAT growth guided at 55-60% over FY26.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 35-40% and PAT margin at 25-30%.
Four H2 FY27 launches planned: Lotus Aurelia, Lotus Sky Plaza, Lotus Portofino and Lotus Odyssey, combined GDV INR3,500-4,000 crore; about 90% approvals in place.
Project-level surplus estimated at about INR9,500 crore over the development cycle; projects expected to complete over the next 4-4.5 years.
Management expects H2 collections to be much better than H1 as projects reach plinth level; FY28 collection guidance to be given at the start of FY28.
Amara and Athena expected to receive OC in FY27 (Amara within the quarter or by March; Athena before March).
capex_capacity: Pipeline of 24 ongoing and upcoming projects, aggregate GDV ~INR20,000 crore, of which 19 are redevelopment-led.
Business development: Lotus Impressa (Shivaji Park, Dadar West), Lotus Stellar (Versova) and Lotus Supremus (Juhu) added in Q2.
INR550 crore of IPO proceeds earmarked for subsidiary (Amalfi, Arcadian, Varun); INR305 crore deployed as of 30 Sep 2026 of INR732 crore net proceeds.
Upfront premium paid to government for new projects in Q2, which management said is to save costs and secure supplier discounts; new projects typically need 8-10% of project cost to start.
GIFT City plot of 5.5 acres on Sabarmati riverfront; expected 1.3-1.5 million sq ft mixed-use development subject to town planning scheme approval.
Lotus Monarch timeline pushed out by one year due to society, trust, Charity Commissioner and government approvals; Ghatkopar (Salona) timeline also extended.
demand_pricing: Management says the luxury segment is less sensitive to RBI's 25 bps repo hike to 5.5% (first hike since early 2023); buyers rely less on home loans.
Mumbai H1 CY2026 sales of homes priced above INR10 crore reached a record INR18,500 crore; prime residential prices up 6.2% YoY per management.
Management says prices have risen across almost all projects in H1 and will rise further as construction progresses if the market supports it.
Management says it is the only suburban player to have completed a commercial redevelopment (Arc One), and has 2-3 more commercial redevelopment projects; about five commercial projects in portfolio.
Prabhadevi (Lotus Aquaria) pricing set at a premium, with 270-degree sea view and ~200 m Art Deco tower; management says no pushback, pre-sales expected to show in next two quarters.
Collections as a share of pre-sales: management said completion-stage projects carry 90-95% balance due, and expects 95-100% collection on three projects completing next year.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are margins above 35% during expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited net debt-free status (no interest burden), minimal marketing spend, a 2.5-3.5 year project cycle that speeds fund deployment, and premium pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected for Trident and what is the commercial redevelopment outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided Trident EBITDA margin at 33-35%, in line with guidance. Management expects commercial redevelopment to carry sustainable margins and cited 2-3 more projects.

qa_highlights.question: How will collections catch up with pre-sales?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said collections are construction-linked: about 5-10% at launch and about 25% at plinth. Of about INR800 crore H1 pre-sales, INR200 crore was collected, and H2 should improve as two of three recent projects move past basement.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term growth beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gives annual guidance only. It pointed to ~INR20,000 crore GDV and ~INR9,500 crore project surplus, with completion over the next 4-4.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did timelines shift for upcoming projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Lotus Monarch moved out by one year due to multiple approving bodies. Ghatkopar (Salona) timeline also extended. Management says overall guidance is unchanged and new projects will replace slipped ones.

qa_highlights.question: Why no Prabhadevi pre-sales, and will the business development outflow constrain the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Prabhadevi is a new micromarket with marketing under way and results expected in two quarters. The INR300 crore outflow was upfront government fees and discounted supplier payments; management said cash is sufficient. Operating cash flow will stay negative in launch periods, though Arcadian is working-capital positive.

risks_watch: Collections lag: Q2 collections of INR60 crore and H1 of INR209 crore against H1 pre-sales of about INR800-879 crore; track whether H2 collections rise as two of three recent projects move past basement to plinth.

Timeline slippage: Lotus Monarch pushed out by one year (society, trust, Charity Commissioner, government approvals) and Ghatkopar (Salona) extended; watch whether replacement projects keep FY27 guidance intact.

Cash deployment: INR305 crore of INR732 crore IPO net proceeds deployed by 30 Sep 2026; management says operating cash flow may stay negative in launch periods, with no FY28 collection guidance until start of FY28.
Prabhadevi (Lotus Aquaria, GDV ~INR800 crore) had no Q2 pre-sales; management expects results in next two quarters at a premium price point.
Delivery of four H2 FY27 launches (combined GDV INR3,500-4,000 crore, about 90% approvals) and the FY27 pre-sales guidance of INR1,800-2,000 crore versus H1 INR879 crore.
key_quotes: Delighted to share that we recorded pre-sales for the quarter at INR470 crores, up 83% year-on-year.
Collections in our business are linked to construction milestones and can vary from quarter -to-quarter.
So, right now, it's not a good time to because we need to evaluate and update you.
So, project-wise, yes, but overall, maybe we cannot give that.
544469|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on sales, margins and launch plans, with the CEO and CFO more cautious and non-committal on collection timing, FY28 numbers and operating cash flow, deferring to the start of FY28 or project-level answers. Management repeatedly stressed the net debt-free balance sheet and construction-linked billing as the reason collections trail pre-sales.

rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin was 39.9% and H1 38.8%, against FY27 guidance of 35-40%; management cites net debt-free status, minimal marketing spend and premium pricing, while Trident is guided at 33-35%, which dilutes the blend.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No unit capacity is measured for a developer; the four H2 FY27 launches (combined GDV INR3,500-4,000 crore, about 90% approvals) and the 24-project pipeline (~INR20,000 crore GDV) are the closest equivalent, but Lotus Monarch slipped one year and GIFT City is subject to town planning approval.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Pre-sales grew 83% YoY in Q2 to INR470 crore and 176% in H1 to INR879 crore, and FY27 revenue and PAT growth of 55-60% is held, with Trident contributing INR178 crore in its first full quarter; Lotus Prabhadevi (GDV ~INR800 crore) has yet to contribute pre-sales.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Three redevelopment projects were added in Q2 and INR305 crore of INR732 crore IPO proceeds is deployed, so further business development is likely but no new capex plan with a date was stated; utilisation is not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated all FY27 guidance rather than raising it, and the H2 ramp required to hit pre-sales of INR1,800-2,000 crore leaves little room for an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 pre-sales of INR879 crore against FY27 guidance of INR1,800-2,000 crore requires a steep H2 ramp, collections were only INR209 crore in H1, and Lotus Monarch and Ghatkopar timelines have slipped.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Four launches are planned for H2 FY27 (Lotus Aurelia, Lotus Sky Plaza, Lotus Portofino, Lotus Odyssey) with combined GDV of INR3,500-4,000 crore and about 90% approvals in place.

rows.label: Collections lag pre-sales; H2 collections expected to improve
rows.why: Collections were INR60 crore in Q2 and INR209 crore in H1 against H1 pre-sales of about INR800-879 crore, and management expects H2 to be much better as projects reach plinth, with about 25% collected at plinth.

rows.label: Net debt-free with INR494 crore net cash
rows.why: Net cash position of INR494 crore at 30 Sep 2026 with the IPO proceeds still INR427 crore undeployed (INR732 crore less INR305 crore).

rows.label: Amara and Athena receive OC in FY27
rows.why: Management expects Amara (within the quarter or by March) and Athena (before March) to receive occupancy certificate, which would convert completed projects into revenue recognition and collections of 95-100% on three completing projects.

tone.note: Management was confident on pre-sales, margins and the four H2 launches, and cautious or deferred on collection timing, FY28 numbers and operating cash flow; analysts probed collections, the INR300 crore business development outflow, Prabhadevi sales traction and timeline slippage.

544470|2026-03.headline: M&B Engineering FY26 revenue rose 27% to INR1,259.7 crores, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 11.9% on forex loss and steel/freight costs; no margin guidance given.
544470|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 27% to INR1,260 crores and PAT rose 20% to INR92.6 crores, but Q4 revenue (INR364 crores, +16%) saw EBITDA flat at INR43 crores and margin down to 11.9% from 14%. Management attributed the margin squeeze to a INR3.9 crore Q4 forex loss (mostly unrealised translation), a 20%+ jump in domestic steel prices, and sharply higher export freight after the Iran conflict; it says adjusted EBITDA excluding forex is about 13%. Volume growth in Phenix was only about 8% in Q4 versus an expected ~15%, due to raw material and gas disruptions in March. Management guided top-line growth of 23-25% for FY27 but declined to give margin guidance.

segments.name: Phenix (PEB)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR985 crores, +29%; export revenue INR165.6 crores. Order book INR871 crores, of which export INR279 crores (32%). Sanand plant utilisation ~75-76% in FY26.

segments.name: Proflex (self-supported roofing)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR275 crores, +23%. Order book INR212 crores. One new unit from UAE commissioned January 2026; two US units expected Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at around 25%; management later cited a 23-25% range, and 20-25% volume growth in PEB and Proflex.
No EBITDA margin guidance for FY27: management cited steel price volatility, uncertain freight, FX and the conflict; will reassess after at least one more quarter.
FY27 export target about INR275-300 crores (around 10,000 tons vs 7,400 tons in FY26); export EBITDA expected 16-17% vs 10-11% domestic at current cost structure.
H1 FY27 expected softer due to Q1 labour availability and Q2 monsoon; H2 historically stronger.
FY27 capex about INR100 crores, including Sanand expansion, part Cheyyar expansion (H2) and maintenance capex.
US sectoral tariff reduced by 25% (effective 6 April per management); benefit partly shared with customers under contract clauses.
capex_capacity: Sanand: adding about 20,000 MT, commissioning expected Q2 FY27, taking capacity to 92,000 MTPA; utilisation expected 65-68% after expansion, peak 75%.
Cheyyar (Tamil Nadu): FY26 utilisation 50-55%; target 68-70% in FY27, with 75% as peak; expansion planned to be operational Q1 or Q2 FY28.
Proflex: installed capacity to rise by about 200,000 sq m p.a. once two US units are commissioned in Q2 FY27.
Volume targets FY27: PEB 85,000-90,000 MT (from ~72,000); Proflex 1.70-1.725 million sq m.
IPO proceeds INR259.32 crores; INR137.81 crores (53%) utilised to 31 March 2026, INR7.5 crores in Q4.
demand_pricing: Order inflow Q4 about INR387-388 crores, down from INR480 crores in Q3 (per analyst); FY26 record inflow INR1,539 crores.
Bid pipeline cited at about INR1,000-1,100 crores across sectors; domestic inquiries in last three months exceeded the prior remaining part of the year.
Export order closures slowing: US cycle time rose from 6-8 weeks to 12-16 weeks amid US inflation and cost pressures.

Steel prices rose about 20%+ in the last quarter (cited INR49,500/t to INR58,500/t); fixed-price contracts with 6-12 month execution; 80-85% of raw material is covered at order booking, 15-20% left open for non-standard items.
New orders being quoted at higher prices; price not locked until advance received. Export freight: a USD 2,000 war surcharge added; cushion built into quotes.
Export realisation about INR2.3-2.7 lakh/t vs domestic about half, driven by US bought-out items costing INR1-2 lakh/t and freight/duties.

qa_highlights.question: How do you see FY27 EBITDA margins given the geopolitical situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide, citing steel price swings (+20% in a quarter), uncertain freight and FX; it will wait at least one more quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export outlook and pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Export target at least INR300 crores in FY27 (vs INR165 crores) per Malav Patel; later cited INR275-300 crores and about 10,000 tonnes; US order closures have slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 volumes grow only ~8% vs ~15% expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material and steel mill disruptions in March (two major suppliers shut, gas shortages); management estimated 10-15% volume lost to the war.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any signs of demand slowdown in PEB?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reports no slowdown in inquiries; warehousing and a gigafactory project cited as ongoing demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the forex loss and what drove the margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: INR3.83 crores is an unrealised translation loss at INR94.78/USD (from INR89-90 post-war); other drivers were export duty, sea freight and US transport costs (INR42-45 crores) and steel price rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% tariff cut passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly; the contract has a tariff sharing clause, so the company keeps part of the benefit and the customer gets part.

risks_watch: Margin visibility: no FY27 margin guidance; steel prices, freight, and FX remain uncontrolled, with 15-20% of raw material open per order.
Sanand 20,000 MT expansion commissioning targeted Q2 FY27; Proflex US units also due Q2 FY27.
Working capital: operating cash flow about negative INR36 crores in FY26 as cash purchases and creditor payments used IPO GCP funds; receivables rose.
Export order conversion slowing (US lead times 12-16 weeks); potential customer deferrals while prices fall.
Supply chain concentration: reliance on one steel supplier when two major mills were shut in March 2026; gas availability constraints.

544470|2026-06.headline: M&B Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.5% to INR291 crores; order book INR1,053 crores, but management withholds FY27 margin guidance for one more quarter.
544470|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew about 22.5% YoY to INR291 crores, with PAT up 22% to INR22 crores. Operating EBITDA was INR33 crores (11.4% margin) against reported EBITDA of INR36 crores. Order on hand stood at INR1,053 crores (up about 25% YoY), though Q1 order inflow of about INR260 crores was softer, which management attributed to large inquiries slipping into Q2. Freight costs (US-bound, roughly 2x to 2.5x since March) and steel prices (up 10-12%) are compressing margins, so management reiterated the 25%+ FY27 revenue growth target but declined to give a margin guide until Q3.

financial_highlights.change: Export ~1,400 MT vs ~INR3 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR1,053 crores (Phenix INR837 crores, Proflex INR216 crores)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1.19 lakh YoY; vs INR1.38 lakh QoQ

segments.name: Phenix (PEB and heavy structural steel)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR214 crores, up 22% YoY; order book INR837 crores including export orders of INR278 crores to be executed mostly in FY27, about 28% dispatched to date. Sanand running at 75-80% utilisation.

segments.name: Proflex (self-supported steel roofing)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR77 crores, up 25% YoY; order book INR216 crores. Installed capacity raised to 21 lakh sq m per annum after commissioning two mobile manufacturing units.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue INR28 crores (about 1,400 MT); management guides about 15% sustainable export EBITDA at current freight, 16-18% in normal freight, versus about 11% domestic. More than 8,000 MT expected in the remaining three quarters.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of over 25% in FY27, implying about INR1,600 crores top line.
No specific FY27 margin guidance; management targets improvement over the current 11-11.5% operating EBITDA margin but will guide at Q2 results (next quarter).
Sanand 20,000 TPA brownfield expansion (PEB capacity 72,000 to 92,000 TPA) commissioning in October 2026, benefits in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Cheyyar brownfield expansion of 20,000 TPA to start this fiscal, completion Q3 FY28; total capacity about 1,54,000-1,55,000 TPA.
Over 20% CAGR over the next three to four years in the medium-term plan, with progressive profitability improvement.
Targeted PEB volume of 85,000-90,000 MT in FY27 versus 72,000 MT last year.

INR30 crores fully automated heavy structural steel processing line at Sanand, adding 10,000 tons to existing 12,000 tons; operational by Q1 FY28. Board approved an additional heavy structural expansion at Sanand.

Cheyyar (South India) is AISC certified, enabling exports to US West Coast via Pacific route from next fiscal; brownfield expansion of 20,000 TPA to complete in Q3 FY28; utilisation targeted at about 60% this fiscal.
Proflex installed capacity 21 lakh sq m per annum after two mobile manufacturing units.
2.5 MW ground-mounted captive solar plant in Gujarat under development.
Third plant site under evaluation in North India; to be announced once finalised.

Hit rate of 12-15% over the last five years, with a stated policy of protecting margins over chasing volume; peers reportedly near 20%.
60-70% of customers are repeat customers.
Freight costs to US roughly 2-2.5x March levels (USD10,000-12,000 per 40ft container); US Section 232 duty cut from 50% to 25%; US steel up about 10-12% since March; domestic freight up 2-5%.
Roughly 80-85% of raw material is booked at order booking; 15-20% is left open to price variation. Domestic PEB margins down 1-2% due to inflation.
Management says domestic market share is about 10-12%, targeting 15% over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 order inflow weak at about INR260 crores versus the INR100 crore/month run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Malav Patel said inflow was up 25% YoY; large inquiries took longer on design freeze and have rubber-banded into Q2. Management says the run rate of about INR100 crores of PEB per month is maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export margin and how much does freight affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Majmudar said the balance INR278 crores export order book yields about 15% EBITDA at peak freight, 16-17% in a better scenario; domestic is about 11%, so the gap has narrowed to about 4-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Phenix realisation per MT fall QoQ to INR1.25 lakh from INR1.38 lakh?
qa_highlights.answer: Keyur Shah attributed it to export mix (under 10%) and project-specific bought-out items, not price cuts; management expects full-year comparability.

qa_highlights.question: Why was domestic PEB realisation flat despite higher steel prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Keyur Shah said domestic tonnage rose about 6.6% and revenue 7.6%; raw material cost was about 0.5% lower YoY and product mix (primary vs sheeting) drove the gap. Higher steel costs will show in orders booked at current prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will Cheyyar capacity come in Q1/Q2 FY28 or Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Malav Patel said the Cheyyar 20,000 TPA expansion comes in Q3 FY28, giving two effective quarters in FY28; Sanand's additional capacity arrives in Q3-Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined a specific range, saying it will give guidance after one more quarter; the target is to improve over the current 11-11.5% operating margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the win rate on bids?
qa_highlights.answer: Chirag Patel said the win rate is 10-12%, up to 12-15% depending on order; large customers take longer to finalise engineering.

risks_watch: FY27 margin guidance deferred to Q2 results; management says it will give specific guidance only after one more quarter, so the 11-11.5% operating EBITDA base is the only reference point for now.

Freight and US tariff exposure: US-bound freight roughly 2-2.5x March levels (USD10,000-12,000 per 40ft container) with management saying freight is unlikely to be sustainable, yet pass-through is incomplete; export margin guided at about 15% at peak freight vs 16-18% normal.

Order inflow pacing: Q1 inflow about INR260 crores; large inquiries have slipped into Q2. Watch whether the roughly INR100 crore per month run rate is maintained against a INR4,000 crore Phenix pipeline and a 12-15% historical hit rate.

Capacity ramp timing: Sanand 20,000 TPA expansion due October 2026 (benefits Q3-Q4 FY27); Sanand heavy structural line by Q1 FY28; Cheyyar 20,000 TPA expansion in Q3 FY28. Any slippage would constrain the 25%+ revenue target and the 85,000-90,000 MT PEB volume goal.

Raw material pass-through: about 80-85% of steel is booked at order booking, with domestic PEB margins already down 1-2% from inflation. Management expects higher steel costs to show up in fresh orders, so the lag between price and margin needs tracking.

544477|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated total income rose 25.6% to INR 633.4 crore and PAT 42.0% to INR 31.8 crore, with a record INR 1,143 crore order book.

qa_highlights.answer: Management views MLFF as positive: it is PPP-based, lowers operator risk, lengthens tenure and reduces competition; no mitigation planned as it sees no issue. Company is studying MLFF opportunities.

544484|2026-03.headline: BlueStone Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 49.1% YoY; SSG of 34% and FY26 revenue of INR 2,441 crore, with 340 stores after 65 added in FY26.
544484|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 standalone revenue up 49.1% YoY and FY26 revenue of INR 2,441 crore, with same-store sales growth of 34% spread evenly across all three months. The store base reached 340 stores in 134 cities after adding 17 stores in Q4 and 65 in FY26, below the 83 added in FY25 and below the RHP plan of 290 stores over FY26-FY27. Management said pre-Ind AS EBITDA margins improved YoY despite a mix shift toward plain gold, and attributed the recovery to rapid entry-level repricing and vertical integration. Gold price inflation inflated closing inventory, which pushed inventory turns down to about 1.13x from 1.3x in FY25.

544484|2026-06.headline: BlueStone Q1 FY27 revenue rose 49% YoY to INR 733 crore, with pre-Ind AS EBITDA up 135% to INR 55 crore and margin at 7.5%.
544484|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 49% YoY to INR 733 crore and pre-Ind AS EBITDA rose 135% to INR 55 crore, lifting operating margin to 7.5% (up 273 bps). Management attributed this to operating leverage despite a custom duty hike on gold from 6% to 15% that softened demand in May before June and July recovered. Same-store sales growth was 39%, repeat revenue share rose to about 60%, while new customer additions reportedly fell from about 50,000 to about 40,000 per quarter, which management tied to merchandise dislocation during the sharp gold rise. Management reiterated a long-term target of roughly INR 12,000 crore revenue in four years, around 30% SSSG and about 20% store distribution growth, though analysts questioned the arithmetic.

The company crossed 1 million customers, opened 27 stores across 7 new cities, and reset entry-level price points, which lowered sequential AOV. 544485|2026-03.headline: Regaal FY26 operating income rose 23.9% to INR 1,134.2 crore and PAT reached INR 55.6 crore; 1,650 TPD expansion commissioned 26 May 2026, with no formal guidance until H1 FY27.

544491|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 34% QoQ to INR112 crores and EBITDA to INR15 crores (13.4% margin), but volumes remain well below last year's Q4.
544491|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed sequential recovery: standalone revenue of INR112 crores (up 34% QoQ) and consolidated revenue of INR110 crores (up 40% QoQ), with standalone PAT rising to INR12 crores from INR4 crores. Year-on-year the quarter was weaker, as US tariff uncertainty cut mint export volumes and utilisation fell to about 60-65% from about 80% a year earlier. The Dahej facility (Krystal Ingredients) commenced commercial production of Gemcool 5 and Safranal on February 26, 2026, while phenol-derivative production was deferred due to phenol price spikes and supply disruption. Management declined to give FY27 guidance, while reiterating FY28 targets of INR1,050-1,100 crores consolidated turnover and 16-18% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 FY26 weaker than Q4 FY25 despite expected restocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said US tariff clarity only came in late February 2026, so Q4 export ramp-up slipped. Management expects this to materialise from the current quarter onwards.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the phenol plant not start, and can phenol be imported?

544491|2026-06.headline: Gem Aromatics Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose to INR83 crore (from INR76 crore) but consolidated EBITDA fell to INR3.3 crore (3.3% margin) and consolidated PAT was a INR7.9 crore loss.
544491|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew about 9% YoY to INR83 crore, with consolidated revenue at INR99 crore versus INR88 crore, helped by a seasonally soft Q1. Margins compressed on product mix, clove raw-material costs after Madagascar floods, and a higher fixed cost base at the new Dahej plant. Consolidated PAT was a loss of INR7.9 crore, pressured by INR9.1 crore of higher depreciation after capitalisation of most of the INR270 crore Dahej capex. Management says the new verticals (cooling agents, Safranal/Citral, phenol derivatives) start contributing from Q2 to Q4 FY27, with FY27 framed as a ramp-up year and no guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the phenol derivatives ramp delayed, and what is the timeline to commercial production?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production by end-Q2 FY27, commercial production in Q3, meaningful revenue from Q4 FY27; pilot batches are approved and customers want plant-level trials. Traders and distributors are being targeted for faster approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Madagascar disruption materially delay the Eugenol ramp, and is clove tree supply structurally at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Port reopened and material is flowing; management expects Eugenol numbers close to plan by year-end. Trees are still productive and sourcing is diversified across Madagascar and East Africa, so no major structural issue foreseen.

qa_highlights.question: How will the business reach sustainable consolidated profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed a timing mismatch: depreciation, interest and manpower costs are already in the P&L while higher-margin Krystal revenue has not yet arrived. Profitability should improve as the new products ramp.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital evolve for Krystal?
qa_highlights.answer: Krystal is synthetic and needs less inventory, so its working cycle should be lower than Gem's; factoring is also being used to reduce debtor days.

qa_highlights.question: Can you quantify the Gemcool orders, and are new products higher margin?

qa_highlights.answer: Mint harvest timing, clove delays and shipping issues pushed revenue into later periods; May-June exports were made but not yet recognised as they had not reached final destinations, with roll-over expected in July-August.

544495|2026-03.headline: NIS Management Q4 FY26 consolidated income rose 13.96% to INR180.03 crore; FY26 PAT hit by INR27.82 crore labour-code provision, adjusted PAT INR19.12 crore.

FY26 consolidated income was INR436.70 crore (up 7.74%) and EBITDA INR33.53 crore (up 12.19%, margin 7.68%, up 30 bps). Reported profitability absorbed a one-time, non-cash exceptional provision of INR27.82 crore for the new Labour Codes; adjusted FY26 PAT was INR19.12 crore and adjusted Q4 PAT INR6.86 crore. Management guided to 12-15% consolidated growth and a target of crossing INR500 crore in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 revenue growth muted, and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone grew about 10% as major contracts came in H2 (Haldia Dock, Reliance Gujarat) with little time to convert. Subsidiary revenue fell due to CCTV stock-outs, exits from low-margin housing-society contracts and delayed West Bengal projects; Keertika Academy fell about INR2 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why are trade receivables high at about INR145 crore and what is the aging?
qa_highlights.answer: NIS Management debtors rose from INR107 crore (H1 start) to INR119 crore in H1 and INR124 crore by year-end, due to collection delays at Haldia Dock, Reliance Gujarat, Patna Secretariat and Irrigation. Debtors were about INR120 crore in April after collections; over 180 days is about INR5 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Has the West Bengal election changed renewals, payments or tenders?

qa_highlights.question: What is the labour-code impact on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contract labour costs are passed through to clients, and no client has sought renegotiation yet. Formalisation may cut informal operators' margins while expanding opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: Why is growth not 30-40% given the small base?
qa_highlights.answer: The MD said faster growth is possible but low-margin, extended-credit tenders would hurt margins, cash flow and DSO. The company wants margins from most contracts before accelerating.

qa_highlights.question: Why are IPO proceeds not fully deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: INR36.91 crore is unutilised. New contracts started only from November to January after the September IPO, and about INR10 crore was deployed and recovered, so full deployment is expected within two years.

qa_highlights.question: When will CCTV revenue rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects better CCTV returns toward year end, with tenders in 2-3 months and 3-4 months of project work, plus AMC contracts for higher margin within about six months.
