544495|2026-06.headline: NIS Management Q1 FY27 consolidated income rose 15.68% YoY to INR115.44 crore, with EBITDA up 36.24% to INR9.22 crore at a 7.99% margin.
544495|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income reached INR115.44 crore, up 15.68% YoY, and EBITDA rose 36.24% to INR9.22 crore with margin up 121 bps to 7.99%. Net profit was INR6.40 crore (up 35% YoY, margin 5.54%), while EPS of INR3.23 grew only 3.53%. Management reiterated the INR500 crore FY27 revenue goal, flagged that the CCTV segment posted a Q1 loss due to project timing, and declined to commit to a margin expansion path beyond 1-2% over two years. Net debt, the share price fall since IPO, and buyback ideas drew pointed investor questions that management largely deflected toward growth investment.

segments.name: Security and manpower (standalone)
segments.commentary: Security revenue INR54.98 crore and housekeeping INR41.88 crore in June 2026 quarter; management cites ~9.95% EBITDA for manpower-type businesses (security, housekeeping, payroll).

segments.name: IFM and payroll
segments.commentary: IFM revenue INR10.28 crore and payroll services INR3.40 crore in the quarter; management says manpower businesses have similar profitability.

segments.name: CCTV and electronic security
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2.11 crore with a loss at PAT level in Q1, attributed to project execution costs ahead of bill raising; management expects stabilisation by September quarter and calls it the most profitable segment. FY26 CCTV loss was about INR1.5 crore.

segments.name: Vocational training (LLP and Keertika Academy)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue nil (INR0 lakh); net loss about INR57 lakh across the LLP and Keertika Academy.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target: cross INR500 crore consolidated, with management saying FY26 Nov-Dec onwards revenues will be booked for the full year, and expecting ~12-15% growth guidance to hold; management ambition of 20% growth stated but not committed.
FY27 EBITDA margin: management says Q1 is seasonally strongest, margins moderate in Q2-Q3 and recover in Q4; no firm FY27 margin expansion number given.
Medium term: Debajit Choudhury expects at least 1-2% EBITDA margin increase over the next two years, driven by electronics and mechanisation mix.
FY28 revenue: Kanad Mukherjee said FY28 will 'definitely cross INR600 crore', with range INR630-640 crore and a target of above INR650 crore by FY28.
CCTV/projects: targeted ~INR30 crore revenue this year (vs INR13-14 crore last year) and PAT of INR3.5-4 crore vs ~INR2.5 crore last year.
Debt: management says no increase in debt; debt levels to stay flat over FY27-FY28.
Free cash flow: average INR8-9 crore over the last 3-4 years; aim to lift to INR13-14 crore by moving systems revenue from INR13-14 crore to ~INR30 crore.
capex_capacity: DDU-GKY Odisha skill project awarded for INR7.93 crore; management expects ~INR4 crore billing this year; about six-month infrastructure gestation period and two-year contract tenor.

HDFC Bank command-and-control centre (CCTV-driven, subscription model, covering 100-150 branches): management expects INR1.5-2 crore investment (about INR1 crore for control room) and INR2-3 crore revenue; final stage negotiations.
Mumbai traffic and police projects: INR15-18 crore expected from one or two tenders; an INR2.18 crore Mumbai traffic tender already received.
NKDA AMC contract worth about INR6 crore expected, pending final tendering; SAIL Burnpur engagement targeted at INR4-5 crore this year.
Acquisitions: management says acquisitions are possible in the future for technology capabilities, but not immediate; no near-term plans for manpower-based acquisitions.
demand_pricing: Q1 order wins: 5 work orders from Reliance Projects and Property Management Services worth INR30.77 crore; 7 Reliance Group FM contracts worth INR14.94 crore (combined INR45.71 crore); 2 Nesco orders worth INR1.94 crore; West Bengal Public Department housekeeping order INR36.71 lakh.
Government GeM tenders now at around 3.85% (L1 pricing); management says it will be more selective in manpower GeM bids and focus on CCTV and DDU-GKY projects.
Customer mix: Reliance top client at INR46-47 crore annually; HDFC Bank ~INR18 crore; Anjali Jewellers ~INR12 crore; airports ~INR30 crore annually; Torrent Power ~INR6-7 crore.
Renewal rates ~96-97%; average client retention 4.5-5 years per management.
Geographic mix: West Bengal ~72-73% of revenue; growth push in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Bihar and Odisha.
Receivable cycle: bills raised after wages; client payment typically in about three months.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 revenues booked from Nov-Dec onwards will be booked for the full year in FY27, and it is confident of crossing INR500 crore this year. Q1 EBITDA is seasonally better, moderating in Q2-Q3 and recovering in Q4, so no margin expansion percentage was committed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 FY27 revenue split by segment and how has the mix changed?
qa_highlights.answer: June 2026 quarter: security INR54.98 crore, housekeeping INR41.88 crore, IFM INR10.28 crore, payroll INR3.40 crore (total INR110.53 crore); CCTV INR2.11 crore; small security and housekeeping INR1.29 crore; vocational training nil. qa_highlights.question: Is 20% growth an aspiration, and how will margins move from ~7% to 8-9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the hope is to grow 20% without compromising the balance sheet, but no commitment. qa_highlights.question: What is net debt, and why not a buyback given the share price fall since the IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone debt about INR69 crore vs cash about INR60 crore as of June; consolidated debt about INR82 crore. qa_highlights.question: Why was CCTV loss-making in Q1 and what is FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Project businesses incur Q1 losses due to execution spend before completion certificates and billing; FY26 CCTV loss was about INR1.5 crore. Management expects stabilisation by September quarter and targets about INR30 crore CCTV/projects revenue and PAT of INR3.5-4 crore this year. FY28: revenue to cross INR600 crore, range INR630-640 crore, target above INR650 crore.

544496|2026-03.headline: Vikran FY26 revenue hit a record INR1,249 crore (vs INR916 crore) with EBITDA margin near 14%; FY27 guided at INR2,200 crore plus.
544496|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR647 crore, up from INR355 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of INR92 crore (14.2% margin) and PAT of INR56 crore (vs INR38 crore). For FY26, revenue rose to INR1,249 crore, EBITDA was about INR175 crore (around 14%) and PAT was INR92 crore (vs about INR78 crore). Management attributed margin dilution to delayed Jal Jeevan Mission receivables (provisioned, mostly in Q4), and to early-stage solar EPC projects. The company closed its acquisition of NOPL Solar (969 MW PM-KUSUM project) at end-April 2026 and guided FY27 revenue of INR2,200 crore plus, with a 14-15% EBITDA margin target.

segments.name: Power T&D
segments.commentary: Management sees FY27 power T&D at about 30% of revenue, focused on selective 765 kV GIS/AIS projects for clients such as Power Grid and NTPC. Scope includes substations, lines, underground cabling and smart metering.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Solar is now the main growth pillar, with management expecting about 60% of FY27 revenue. Marquee wins include 100 MW AC (Ellume Energy), 400 MW AC / 580 MWp DC (NTPC Renewable) and 600 MW (NOPL Solar); 20 MW of NOPL is commissioned, with more due by end-May.

segments.name: Water infrastructure
segments.commentary: Water is about 10% of FY27 revenue from the existing order book, roughly INR600 crore; no new water bids for about 18 months. Jal Jeevan Mission receivables are about INR400 crore, and INR17-18 crore was received in FY27 to date.

segments.commentary: Acquired 100% at end-April 2026; project cost INR4,200 crore with sanctioned lender funding. Management cites revenue over INR500 crore over 25 years, 85-88% EBITDA margin, and about INR1 crore per month from the first 20 MW.

Possible additional INR1,000-1,400 crore solar EPC order from the Onix balance EPC scope, not yet in the INR5,700 crore order book; may be booked at arm's length price.

Data centre EPC target of about INR100 crore order book in FY27, initially 50-100 MW.
MNRE and MSEDCL have extended the NOPL project deadline to March 2027.

Project funding of INR4,200 crore is sanctioned by a major lender, and the existing financing line rolls over to the new owner subject to a promoter evaluation; backup financing is in place.
Solar EPC: 500 MW EPC project in execution; company's total under-construction portfolio stated as about 1.5 GW (1 GW developer, 500 MW EPC).
Operational footprint: 22 states, 190 locations, about 1,200 staff, with about 222 at the Thane head office.
Management is cautiously evaluating Middle East and Africa opportunities, and says it is not pursuing a developer or investment model for data centres.
demand_pricing: Government push and private demand for solar; management sees better cash flow and margins in solar.
Management said it is selectively bidding; no new water orders for about 18 months.
Management said the company has no BESS in its current scope but has bid for some BESS projects.
Supply chain is largely dependent on China, but management says procurement was front-loaded in FY26 and the West Asia conflict has had limited impact so far.
Management says CFO-level margin for FY23-25 was 15-17%, and that projects are being chosen for similar margin range.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin recover from 13-14% to historical 18-22%, and what is the status of the Onix project and its financing?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY23-25 EBITDA was 15-17%, with FY26 at about 14% due to JJM receivable provisions (reversed on collection). Management said the Onix SPV is now 100% owned; the lender is comfortable, and 4 projects are commissioned with 2 more due by end-May.

qa_highlights.question: What is execution in FY27 with and without NOPL, and what milestones have been achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says INR2,200 crore plus is achievable with or without NOPL, and that a plan without NOPL 'does not make a lot of sense'. Milestones since the April takeover are limited to a few commissioned projects; land and evacuation issues are cleared.

qa_highlights.question: How much receivables exposure is there from water/JJM, and how much was provided in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR400 crore of water receivables are due from JJM. About INR20 crore of provision was taken in FY26, mostly in Q4; the CFO said there is no specific high-risk receivable.

qa_highlights.question: When will cash flow turn positive, and will there be equity dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there are no plans for further equity dilution and that operating cash flow is expected to turn positive from FY28; the order book has grown from about INR2,000 crore to over INR5,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue mix for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said about 60% solar, 30% power T&D and about 10% water.

qa_highlights.question: Is the additional INR1,400 crore NOPL solar order included in the INR5,700 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not included because the order is not yet placed and documentation is pending; the CFO said about INR1,000 crore may be booked in coming days, executable over 12-15 months.

NOPL execution: about 85% land identified, 150-odd locations to complete by March 2027 deadline; the lender line roll-over is subject to a promoter evaluation.
Pending INR1,000-1,400 crore Onix balance EPC order (arm's length pricing) that would be additional to the INR5,700 crore order book.
Supply-chain and geopolitical risk from China sourcing and the West Asia conflict; management is hedging with large suppliers.
Data centre EPC entry, with a small INR100 crore target; no formal order yet.

rows.why: Management said operating cash flow is expected to turn positive from FY28, but it remains negative today with receivables about INR1,000 crore against payables of INR788 crore.

544497|2026-06.headline: Anlon Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin fell to ~17% (PAT ₹8.28 cr) on raw-material spikes and Remember India consolidation; management targets 25-27% for FY27.
544497|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Q1 FY27 total income was ₹87.62 cr versus ₹33.31 cr in Q1 FY26, with EBITDA of ₹15.65 cr (vs ₹6.26 cr) and PAT of ₹8.28 cr (vs ₹3.55 cr). EBITDA margin moderated to about 17%, which management attributed to a sharp rise in solvent and petrochemical raw-material prices after the geopolitical conflict and to operating costs of the newly acquired Remember India Health links being consolidated. The company completed the 63.98% acquisition of Remember India on 8 May 2026, has acquired Apiqo Organics and Bizotic Lifesciences, and is moving into finished dosage formulations. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of ₹350-400 cr and a ~30% three-year revenue CAGR, but gave limited quantitative detail on Remember India.

financial_highlights.change: moderated; management earlier guided ~24-25% floor for Q1

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue contribution, Q1 FY27 - Anlon standalone
financial_highlights.change: management cited standalone sales of ₹30 cr vs ₹33 cr in analyst question

segments.name: Anlon Healthcare (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ~₹30-32 cr, down from ₹33 cr YoY per analyst; management says it is at peak utilisation and expects FY27 standalone revenue of ~₹180 cr. Production cycles of 30-45 days mean some output lands in Q2.

segments.name: Apiqo Organics (68% stake, moving to 100%)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ~₹45 cr, described as the most profitable unit; FY27 revenue expected ₹120-150 cr. Business is fully booked in industrial and fine chemicals; share-swap to make it a 100% subsidiary to complete by end-Q2.

segments.name: Bizotic Lifesciences (57% stake, moving to 100%)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ~₹12 cr; FY27 expected ~₹60 cr. Management says it is profitable and that committed partner business exists; share-swap to 100% also targeted by end-Q2.

segments.name: Remember India Health links (63.98%)
segments.commentary: Finished dosage formulations (tablets, capsules, ointments) with access to 30+ dossiers; in investment and turnaround phase. No revenue assumed for FY27 until at least Q4 FY27; WHO-PQ approval expected by end-CY2026. Margin expected above 25%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of ₹350-400 cr reiterated; management said H1 comparison is the right lens, and the guidance range was re-confirmed as ₹380-400 cr in one answer.
EBITDA margin: ~17% in Q1; management expects margins to improve from Q2 (said 'better than the first quarter') and target 25-27% for FY27 on consolidated basis; earlier comment of 22-25% in H1.
Gross margin expected to hold at 40-45%.
FY28 revenue indicated at ~₹700 cr if Anlon-site expansion (~₹130 cr capex, ~1,200 MT additional) is commissioned on schedule by Q1 FY28; management flagged possible delays from statutory approvals.

Working capital: receivable days expected to fall toward 60-70 days over time (current ~130-135 days vs 90-day terms); management expects positive operating cash flow in FY27, 'lower but positive'. Management also said H1 operating cash flow positive is targeted before year-end.
Biologics subsidiary (Anlon Biologics) revenue expected from Q4 FY28; Anlon Medicare from Q2 FY28; Remember India peak revenue/EBITDA to be detailed in Q2 call.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity after three acquisitions stated at ~1,400-1,600 MT per annum; management clarified Anlon standalone is ~400 MT and is at peak.
Anlon-site expansion: ~₹130 cr capex adding ~1,200 MT (standalone to ~1,600 MT); commissioning targeted by Q1 FY28 subject to statutory approvals.
Funding: ~₹70 cr debt at ~8.5-8.6% interest; balance from internal accruals.
Eight new cleanrooms planned at the new facility to run eight APIs in parallel; initial planning assumes 50-60% utilisation.
Bizotic and Apiqo utilisation can rise gradually from ~65% toward higher levels; no 65-to-85% jump expected within this year.
Anlon Biologics (peptides, biosimilars) construction to begin within ~2 months; in-house peptide manufacturing targeted by FY28.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices: management said solvent/methanol-linked inputs rose 2-3x since pre-war (methanol cited at ₹22 to ₹58-60/kg); not yet normalised. Around 40% of API manufacturing cost is solvents and petroleum-linked inputs.

Price pass-through: price increases on finished products have been initiated and customers have agreed; management expects this to reflect over the next one to two quarters, but earlier orders at old prices weighed on Q1.
Customer base is concentrated: 10-15 B2B customers, which limits ability to reprice frequently.
Fine/specialty chemicals (Apiqo): fully booked, described as 'overbooked'; management estimates ₹120-150 cr contribution in FY27.
CDMO: expected commercial supply of first molecule by Q3 and others by Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28; process validations ongoing.
Seven new APIs/DMFs planned for filing within FY27; compilation under way.

qa_highlights.question: Have raw material prices normalised, and by which quarter will EBITDA margins recover? Will Q2 margins be similar to Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: RM prices not normalised; solvent/methanol-linked inputs up 2-3x (methanol ~₹22 to ₹58-60/kg). Management expects margin normalisation by Q3 and said Q2 would be better than Q1, with price increases reflecting over one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue outlook versus ~₹87 cr Q1 run-rate and capacity utilisation (~62%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated ₹350-400 cr as peak-level potential and said utilisation is ~65-70%; asked to compare H1 rather than quarter-on-quarter because production cycles run 15-40+ days.

qa_highlights.question: Segment revenue contribution in Q1 and expected FY27 split?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1: Apiqo ~₹45 cr, Anlon standalone ~₹32 cr, Bizotic ~₹11.5-12 cr. FY27 expectations: Apiqo ₹120-150 cr, Anlon standalone ~₹180 cr, Bizotic ~₹60 cr; Remember India not included until Q3/Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why has EBITDA margin declined over the last two quarters, and what is the FY27 consolidated margin expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to temporary geopolitical RM spike with customers on prior-price orders, plus lower-margin acquired units and Remember India costs. Management guided 25-27% consolidated EBITDA for FY27 and said Q2 would sustain around 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Expected Remember India revenue and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: No FY27 revenue assumed; WHO-PQ approval expected by end-CY2026; detailed projection deferred to Q2 call. Management said margins should be above 25% due to in-house API backward integration.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital, receivable days and operating cash flow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables run ~130-135 days versus 90-day terms; management expects reduction toward 60-70 days over time and 'lower but positive' operating cash flow in FY27, targeted before year-end. Inventory is development stock held 9-12 months pending DMF approval.

qa_highlights.question: Interest rate on the ~₹70 cr debt and PAT margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt cost ~8.5-8.6%; PAT margin guided at ~12-13% for FY27 and ~11-13% for FY28, described as conservative and sensitive to statutory approval delays.

Remember India: no FY27 revenue assumed; WHO-PQ approval targeted by end-CY2026; peak revenue and EBITDA to be detailed only in Q2 call.
Capacity expansion: ~₹130 cr Anlon-site capex (~1,200 MT) targeted by Q1 FY28 but subject to statutory approvals; management flagged possible delays of one to two months changing projections.
Working capital and cash flow: receivable days of ~130-135 vs 90-day terms; management suggests a possible fundraise may be needed for the FY28 revenue ambition, which it did not confirm.

Guidance consistency: management gave differing EBITDA margin ranges (25-27%, 25-28%, 25-30%) and revenue framing; watch Q2 for reconciliation and the share-swap completion of Apiqo and Bizotic to 100% by end-Q2.

544497|2026-09.headline: Anlon Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 102.3% YoY to INR105.61 crore, with EBITDA margin recovering to 23.9%.
544497|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR105.61 crore, up 102.3% YoY, and H1 FY27 revenue of INR193.17 crore already exceeds full-year FY26 revenue. EBITDA margin recovered to 23.9% in Q2 from 17.8% in Q1, which management attributes mainly to passing raw material costs on to customers through price revisions. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR380-400 crore and gave FY28 guidance of INR650-700 crore, excluding medical devices and CDMO upside. Operating cash outflow narrowed to INR7.94 crore in H1 FY27 from INR79.44 crore for all of FY26, and the company is targeting positive operating cash flow by end-FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Over 600 bps QoQ recovery from 17.8% in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash used in operating activities (H1 FY27)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR79.44 crore for full FY26

segments.name: Anlon Healthcare (standalone)
segments.commentary: Contributed 44.6% of H1 FY27 consolidated revenue; within it, intermediates were 81.1% and API 17.1%, with the balance nutraceuticals and other products. Standalone utilisation is 85-86%.

segments.name: Apiqo Organics
segments.commentary: Contributed 43.7% of H1 FY27 consolidated revenue; has opened an industrial and fine chemicals vertical as a new revenue stream outside pharma. Management cites a sustainable EBITDA margin of 20-23% and PAT margin of 11-13%.

segments.name: Bizotic Lifescience
segments.commentary: Contributed 11.7% of H1 FY27 consolidated revenue; provides ready-to-operate API capacity at a second manufacturing site. Share swap to take the company to 100% ownership was said to be completing within 8-10 days.

segments.name: Anlon Medicos (formulations, formerly Remember India)
segments.commentary: Entered finished dosage formulations (tablets, capsules) with access to over 30 formulation dossiers; operations start from Q3 FY27. Management expects first revenue in Q4 FY27 and sees a tablet/capsule peak of INR80-90 crore.

segments.name: Anlon Biologics and Anlon Medico (new subsidiaries)
segments.commentary: Both incorporated in the period. Anlon Biologics targets peptides, oligonucleotides and biosimilars, with first revenue in Q4 FY28; Anlon Medico targets surgical implants and devices, with first revenue from Q3 FY28 and INR70-80 crore expected within 3 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance reiterated at INR380-400 crore; management said it is almost in line with that target.
FY28 revenue guidance of INR650-700 crore (INR680-700 crore in a later answer), excluding medical devices and CDMO upside.
Sustainable EBITDA margin target of 25-28%; current run-rate is 23-24%. Management said FY27 full-year margin could reach 25-26%, and FY28 is 'very early to commit'.
Long-run consolidated sustainable EBITDA margin of 23-25% and PAT margin of 11-13%, per management's segment-weighted view.
Positive operating cash flow targeted by end-FY27. Working capital cycle nominal target of 170-180 days; receivable days are being cut to 90-100 from 130-140.
Dividend decision deferred; management will review cash availability and free cash flow around Q4 FY27 results.
Capital raise of up to INR250 crore being finalised by end-November, subject to AGM approval; INR65-70 crore term loan planned for capex.
capex_capacity: Group installed capacity is about 1,900-2,000 MTPA against 400 MTPA at the Anlon parent facility; consolidated utilisation is 65-67%, expected to stay flat for the next two quarters.

Rajkot greenfield expansion adds about 1,200 MTPA via 8 new clean lines, targeted for Q1 FY28 (construction on track; a public hearing in December could cause a 1-2 month delay). Expansion of 500 MTPA planned across the group; Apiqo's 500-600 MTPA expansion is also due by Q1 FY28.
Of the INR130 crore expansion capex, only INR15-20 crore has been spent so far; maximum spend expected by December as advances are paid to suppliers.
Anlon Medicos injectable facility expansion has started, with injectables expected by end-FY28.
CDMO: 3 molecules for 2 global innovators; first molecule commercial supply slipped to end-Q3 or early Q4 FY27 from Q3 FY27. Other two in validation with commercialisation after H1 FY28 (6-8 months).
demand_pricing: Price revisions passed through to customers were the main driver of margin recovery; raw material prices are not normalised and remain near post-March war levels.
Standalone API vs intermediate mix is about 20:80 by revenue; management says API and intermediate both run at about 35% gross margin.

Portfolio is 21 DMFs filed; 4 products already commercialised and validated among the 7 targeted for FY27. 3 filings planned by December and the rest by February-March; one filing may slip 1-2 months.
Ketoprofen US DMF is on hold pending a US FDA trigger from a customer; no plan to file directly for the US.
Management claims cost is 10% or more below Chinese prices for its key molecules and that it has displaced Chinese suppliers in Europe, LATAM, Japan and Korea.
Loxoprofen topical gel for India: CDSCO/DCGI approval expected by at least Q1 FY28; management says revenue could be 2-3x the tablet/capsule level once launched pan-India.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 revenue reach about INR400 crore, and what is the FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guidance remains INR380-400 crore, almost on track. FY28 is guided at INR650-700 crore, based on existing projects and the expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins stay within 25-30% and when does Anlon Medicos start revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Current run-rate is 23-24%, with a sustainable 25-27% targeted; FY28 is early to commit. Anlon Medicos first revenue was pushed to Q4 FY27 because of re-registration and takeover approval delays.

qa_highlights.question: Has the CDMO commercial supply started?
qa_highlights.answer: Not yet; the first molecule commercial supply is delayed 1-2 months to end-Q3 or early Q4 FY27. Molecules 2 and 3 are validated but commercialisation will take 6-8 months, after H1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins rise 600 bps QoQ, and what is the working capital plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly price pass-through to customers, as raw materials have not normalised. Nominal working capital cycle is 170-180 days; receivable collection is improved to 90-100 days from 130-140 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is capacity utilisation and what is the medical device contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated utilisation is 65-67%; standalone is 85-86%. Medical devices are excluded from FY28 projections and are expected to reach INR70-80 crore in 3 years at EBITDA above 25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the purpose of the capital raise and how is capex funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Up to INR250 crore is being finalised for capex in parent and subsidiaries, including Anlon Biologics. Separately, INR65-70 crore term loan is planned, with the balance from internal accruals.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on continued price pass-through, and raw material costs remain elevated; sustainable margin is still below the 25-28% target.
Capacity expansion timing: Rajkot's 1,200 MTPA line and Apiqo's expansion are targeted for Q1 FY28 but depend on a December public hearing and regulatory approvals.
Working capital remains stretched: receivable days about 123 (annualised) and payable days about 40; debt has risen, and management did not give a deadline for the INR65-70 crore term loan.
CDMO and Anlon Medicos revenue timing has slipped repeatedly; the first CDMO commercial supply is now expected late in Q3 or early Q4 FY27.
Governance and disclosure: an analyst questioned audit coverage across subsidiaries, and management's answer was that consolidated numbers were also reviewed, which needs verification.
Dividend intent is undecided, and the INR250 crore fundraise details are not finalised.
544497|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the top line and Q2 margin recovery, but cautious and hedged on forward margins, CDMO timing and FY28 specifics. Management repeatedly says it is 'very early to commit' and gave a few inconsistent answers, including the FY28 revenue range and the Anlon Medicos start quarter.
key_quotes: Our EBITDA margin for Q2 FY27 recovered to 23.9%, an improvement of over 600 basis points sequentially.
Majorly, we have passed on the cost to the customer. Because raw material prices are not normalized yet.

So, we are just focusing on the products where we are strong in terms of the chemistry, where we are strong in handling of the hazardous and poisonous material, which can give us the leverage against the China.

rows.why: Anlon Medicos formulations start from Q3 FY27 with first revenue expected Q4 FY27 (tablet/capsule peak INR80-90 crore); Loxoprofen topical gel approval expected by at least Q1 FY28; CDMO first commercial supply end-Q3 or early Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Positive operating cash flow by end-FY27
rows.why: H1 FY27 operating cash outflow narrowed to INR7.94 crore from INR79.44 crore in all of FY26, and receivable days are being cut to 90-100 from 130-140.

rows.label: Bizotic share swap to 100% ownership
rows.why: Share swap said to be completing within 8-10 days, taking the company to 100% ownership of Bizotic (11.7% of H1 FY27 revenue).

rows.why: Re-registration and takeover approval delays pushed first formulation revenue to Q4 FY27, and management has not given a firm date beyond that.

tone.note: Management was confident on top-line growth and the Q2 margin rebound but cautious on forward margins, CDMO timing and FY28 specifics, often saying it was 'very early to commit'; analysts pressed on the FY28 range, margin targets, working capital and audit coverage across subsidiaries.

544501|2026-03.headline: Sugs Lloyd FY26 revenue rose about 70% to INR300 crore, PAT up 71% to INR28 crore, with INR825 crore unexecuted order book.
544501|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue reached INR300 crore versus INR176 crore in FY25, ahead of the INR270 crore guidance, with EBITDA up 69% and PAT up 71% to about INR28 crore. Management said margins were held broadly flat year-on-year, though Q4 margin was about 12% versus roughly 14% for the half year, which management attributed to a delayed MAHAGENCO order and related site disruption. Growth drivers were RDSS-funded transmission and distribution work and solar EPC, plus a INR640 crore (incl. 18% GST, about INR540 crore ex-GST) SCADA order from Konkan Railway. Receivables and retention balances rose, and management flagged 40% of FY26 sales coming in Q4 as a key working-capital issue.

up 71% YoY (from about INR16 crore); PAT margin retained

INR125 crore (INR65 crore non-fund, INR60 crore fund-based)

segments.commentary: INR110 crore of unexecuted order book; about 52% of FY26 revenue per analyst citation.

Of the INR640 crore order, management expects INR200-250 crore billing in FY27, with the balance in FY28.

Compact FPI launch by Q2 FY27; VCB (switchgear) likely next year; RMUs further out pending CPRI and ERDA type testing.

Working on SCADA-compatible grids, ADMS, DMS and distributed automation projects; bidding on about INR1,225 crore of tenders at various stages, with about 3,000 tenders identified for bid preparation.
No specific capacity or capex figures were given in the call.

Tender strike rate estimated at 20-30%, implying 200-300 of the INR1,225 crore tenders could be won.
Payment terms on RDSS project: 60% on material supply, 30% on installation and commissioning, 10% retention released after completion against bank guarantee.
Most orders carry price variation clauses covering commodity (including LME-linked copper) and statutory tax changes.

Competitors named for large SCADA projects: L&T, Voltas and other EPC players. Management said 99% of business is with government entities, and it is bidding only on centrally or multilaterally funded projects.
Geographic expansion: Odisha and Bihar were earlier core markets; now Gujarat, Maharashtra, Punjab, Chhattisgarh; international expansion planned but not immediate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 'other current assets' jump to INR42 crore, and is it retention money?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it is retention money not yet due, released after the company discharges project obligations.

qa_highlights.question: How will receivables be managed, and what are the terms, working capital and margins on the large INR600 crore order?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 40% of sales fall in Q4, with 10% carried from prior periods. Steps include a collection task force, shifting to projects with easier payment terms, and capping retention at 10%. The large order is expected to carry no margin pressure, under RDSS payment terms.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins be maintained on the new project pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins broadly similar, with quarterly variation from product and customer mix; FY26 margin levels expected to hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margin fall to about 12%?

Price revision initiated about 20-25 days before the call with no customer resistance reported; for a 100 ml container the price increase is about 5.5-6% of selling price.

Management said power costs have fallen because of solar, and that polymer price pass-through typically lags, with price cuts on reversal expected to be partial (e.g., INR2 rise may reverse by INR0.75-1).

Indian IV fluid demand growing 8-10% YoY, ~INR185 crore market per management's estimate; two-port segment expected to grow 12-13%. SteriPort demand estimated at 20-25 crore bottles, rising to 75-80 crore bottles by 2030; management targets 20-25% share.

Marketing and Finance/HR run AI end-to-end. It said the margin benefit has started to show but there is a long way to go.

qa_highlights.question: How much cash burn is there, and how will working capital be funded in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital build is from EPC execution and growth, with bills deducted at once; it expects to use bank debt, says banks are willing to lend, and cited sufficient cash and bank balance. No specific debt quantum was given.

qa_highlights.question: What EPC revenue and margin are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 EPC revenue about INR30 crores; FY27 minimum INR200 crores. EPC margin around 8%, which management later said was PAT margin.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new products deliver double-digit margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins better than existing products and said it expects double-digit, without a firm number until sales begin.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise from INR4 crores to INR24 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to EPC startup expenses, with related invoices still pending.

qa_highlights.question: Is infrastructure/EPC a recurring business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, it will be recurring, and that EPC is forward integration because electrification works need cables and conductors.

risks_watch: Negative operating cash flow in FY26 (analysts cited about INR70-74 crores) and rising inventory and receivable days, with working capital cycle of about 110-120 days cited by an analyst; management did not give a figure.
Rising debt: management expects bank borrowing to fund working capital and EPC, with no quantum disclosed.
Margin visibility: management cited similar margins but gave no segment-level margin guidance for EPC versus cables; the EPC margin was ambiguous between EBITDA and PAT.
Commissioning delays: power connection for the conductor division is still pending, and BIS licences for new products may delay full utilisation.
Tender conversion: about INR1,000 crores bid with no conversion ratio given and no prior T&D tender experience.

544525|2026-03.headline: GK Energy FY26 standalone revenue rose 40% to INR 1,532.54 crore, with EBITDA margin at 20.44% and PAT at INR 201 crore.
544525|2026-03.overview: FY26 standalone revenue crossed INR 1,500 crore for the first time, up 40% YoY, with EBITDA of INR 313 crore (20.44% margin vs 18.64%) and PAT of INR 201 crore (up 51%). Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 418.57 crore (vs INR 352 crore YoY), EBITDA INR 85.96 crore and PAT INR 59.05 crore. Installations of 61,000+ systems in FY26 (up 34%) fell short of the 70,000-75,000 guidance, which management attributed to rainfall in Maharashtra and raw material delays in late March. Net cash stood at INR 240 crore against net debt of INR 155 crore a year earlier, while working capital days rose to about 140-150 days.

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,715 crore; EBITDA INR 318 crore; PAT INR 204.3 crore

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 352 crore in Q4 FY25; about 6-7% below Q3 per analyst
vs net debt of INR 155 crore in FY25

financial_highlights.value: About 140-150 days (management cited 112 days at one point; 183 days in H1 FY26)
INR 710 crore (as of 31 March plus orders received after April 2026, including INR 350 crore Magel Tyala Phase 4 order)

segments.name: Solar pumps (PM-KUSUM component B / Magel Tyala)
segments.commentary: Core business, asset-light EPC model with OEM/ODM sourcing. Maharashtra share cited at 15%+ and national share at 8-9%; management says Maharashtra will remain the main focus until Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Rooftop (PM Surya Ghar / Smart Scheme)
segments.commentary: Early-stage, with more than 5 MW installed so far. Smart Scheme (1 kW, Maharashtra) is targeted at 1 lakh households at possibly lower margins; working capital is lower for Surya Ghar (cash-and-carry) and Smart Scheme runs under a ULA model with direct government payment.

segments.name: Solar cell subsidiary (DCR cells)
segments.commentary: Wholly-owned subsidiary did INR 199 crore of business in FY26 to secure DCR cell supply; long-term contract for 875 MW for the current financial year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target: roughly double FY26 volume to 120,000-140,000 pumps, with pump revenue of INR 2,200-2,400 crore and rooftop revenue of INR 600-1,000 crore, for a total of about INR 3,000 crore plus.
Management expects to keep EBITDA margin at two digits and to try for double-digit net margin; for FY27 EBITDA a 10-15% variation was called possible, though management said it was too early to say.
Analyst's worst case discussed on the call: about INR 2,500 crore revenue and INR 250 crore PAT if PM-KUSUM 2.0 is delayed; management did not confirm this figure.
Management expects to win about INR 1,400 crore of orders by end of Q1 FY27 (INR 700 crore in hand plus INR 700 crore expected from Magel Tyala Phase 5 and Smart Scheme).
Working capital is expected to stay around 140-150 days, with a long-term aim to reduce it; inventory days are down to 21.
Management will consider providing separate EBITDA guidance for the EPC and solar cell trading businesses.
capex_capacity: Monthly installation capacity is about 15,000+ systems, built through OEM/ODM long-term agreements, with the company stating it incurs no manufacturing capex.
Company dropped solar module manufacturing plans and is sourcing modules, pumps, motors and controllers under brand-labelled supply from partners in Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, UP and Kerala.

Fixed assets rose by about INR 100 crore, mainly from a corporate office (about INR 90 crore per the analyst's question), which management said was bought in place of fixed deposits used to secure bank limits.
Company has more than 1,300 field staff and covers more than 7,500 villages; cumulative renewable installations total 617 MW.
Management has no plans to enter new states in FY27; current states are UP, Haryana, Rajasthan, MP, Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is intact and that Q4 shortfall was due to rainfall and late-March raw material disruption linked to the war that started in late February.
Competitive intensity is high in pump supply: management described solar pumps as a commodity, but EPC is less competitive and brand recall with farmers matters.
Management says GK does not bid below its required margin, and that lower unit prices are offset by volume and vendor renegotiation.
Raw material risk is managed through six-month forward price freezes and 30-50% capacity commitments with 2-3 suppliers per product.
Magel Tyala Phase 5 is under evaluation and expected to open; PM-KUSUM 2.0 timing has slipped from early April to end-June per the analyst, and management said specifications are being revised.
Management did not bid on the Karnataka tender in January, citing a need to be sure of funds and demand before entering a state.
Receivables from some large state utilities improved in H2 FY26; management expects the cycle to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 installations (about 17,000) and FY26 volumes miss the roughly 50,000 H2 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is intact and blamed raw material delays and late-March rainfall in Maharashtra; FY26 volume was 60,000+ against 70,000+ guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold given raw material price pressure and competition in tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited forward procurement contracts with price freezes for 3-6 months and volume-driven cost gains, and said it aims to keep the two-digit margin.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 targets and funding plan for the working capital needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to roughly double volumes, with about INR 3,000 crore revenue, and said it will use equity raised in October, surplus reserves, and unutilised CC and BG bank limits; it gave no cost figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the corporate office purchase a concern for an asset-light company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the office was bought with fixed deposits that had been used to secure bank limits, so the cash was moved into an asset.

qa_highlights.question: How much of PM-KUSUM 2.0 can GK capture?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put its national share at about 9% and its Maharashtra share at 15%+; it expects PM-KUSUM 2.0 volumes to be two to three times the earlier scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company disclose Q1 FY27 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a quarterly number and said it would talk only on an annual basis.

risks_watch: PM-KUSUM 2.0 timing: management said it expects volume from Q3 FY27, and an analyst cited a deferral from early April to end-June.
Working capital at about 140-150 days with a rising receivables and bank-limit need, implied by the FY27 INR 3,000 crore target.
Competitive pricing in Magel Tyala and rising tender competition, with management saying realisation is under pressure.
Raw material and geopolitical risk, with management saying a 10-15% EBITDA variation is possible.
Governance: an investor asked for more frequent investor engagement, and no post-Q3 call was held. Management said it would consider this.

544525|2026-06.headline: GK Energy Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 71.1% YoY to INR 505 crore, with PAT up 61.6% to INR 59.7 crore.
544525|2026-06.overview: GK Energy reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue, with standalone revenue of INR 505 crore (up 71.1% YoY), EBITDA of INR 86.1 crore (margin 17.05%, up 47.7%) and PAT of INR 59.7 crore (up 61.6%). Order book stood at INR 541 crore as of June/early August 2026, including orders received after June. Installations more than doubled to 24,118 systems, and 109 MW of renewable capacity was commissioned, taking the cumulative base to over 164,500 systems and 726 MW. Management reiterated FY27 revenue doubling and PAT in double digits, with the PM-KUSUM 2.0 tender expected in Q3 as the key dependency.

segments.commentary: About 95% of current revenue and about 80% of the order book, per management. Realisation per pump fell YoY while volumes grew close to double.

Competition was acknowledged as a factor in lower per-pump realisation, but no competitor was named.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 541 crore order book enough for doubling FY27 revenue, and is margin compression expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of the doubling track, with Magel Tyala Phase 6/7 and PM-KUSUM 2.0 and rooftop as drivers. It guided PAT to stay at the Q1 level for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and timing of PM-KUSUM 2.0?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q3 FY27 is the expected timing and that work should start by end-Q3. It said the press release on subsumed funds related to a legislative-assembly answer, not PM-KUSUM 2.0.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company reach about INR 3,000 crore revenue in the remaining three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is usually 15-20% of annual volume and Q4 35-40%, so the back-end-loaded pattern supports the target. It said growth would be 'slightly plus/minus' the Q1 rate.

qa_highlights.question: Why did realisation per pump fall while volumes doubled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed lower realisation per pump but higher total volume. It expects realisation to stay flat unless PM-KUSUM 2.0 specifications change.

qa_highlights.question: Is backward integration planned as part of the USD 1 billion by 2030 vision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not clear on backward integration, since manufacturing capacity already exists in the market. It said further product additions are under consideration and PM-KUSUM is one of several drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest expense fall from INR 11 crore to INR 5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited surplus cash from strong receivables in FY26 and IPO proceeds used for working capital, with no bank debt. It said the INR 5 crore level will persist.

544525|2026-09.headline: GK Energy H1 FY27 revenue rose 38.9% to INR 907.8 crore, with Q2 revenue up 12.3% to INR 402.7 crore and receivables still stretched at 204 days.
544525|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue grew 38.9% to INR 907.8 crore, EBITDA rose 21.6% to INR 160.5 crore at a 17.7% margin, and PAT grew 30.7% to INR 109 crore. Q2, seasonally the weakest quarter, saw revenue up 12.3% to INR 402.7 crore, EBITDA of INR 74.4 crore (18.5% margin) and PAT of INR 49.4 crore. Management highlighted INR 377.5 crore of customer collections since 30 September, which cut receivable days from 204 to about 128 on its calculation. The company is widening from solar pumps into rooftop solar and its first utility-scale BESS order (150 MW / 300 MWh).

financial_highlights.change: about 128 days after INR 377.5 crore collected since 30 Sep

segments.name: Solar pumps (agriculture)
segments.commentary: Q2 installations of 19,391 systems (up 41.8% YoY) and 84 MW commissioned (up 33.3%). H1 installations 43,509 (up 77.6%) and 193 MW commissioned (up 70.8%). Additional institutional order of 14,000 off-grid pumps in Maharashtra received October 2026.

segments.name: Retail and institutional rooftop solar
segments.commentary: Management says retail rooftop is growing strongly; more than 2,000 systems installed and 4,000-5,000 system demand cited. Institutional order to install one lakh rooftop systems; an order of around INR 450 crore was referenced on the call.

segments.name: BESS (battery storage, utility-scale)
segments.commentary: First order for 150 MW / 300 MWh utility-scale installation. Company plans to build its own BESS plants and sell power to DISCOMs under a fixed-revenue model for 15 years; intends to expand to 2 GW in the midterm.

Year-end FY27 receivable days guided at 120-150 days.
Rooftop margins expected slightly below pump margins; rooftop working capital cycle 45-60 days.

Cumulative base above 1,84,000 systems and over 800 MW across India; network of six states, 7,500+ villages, 20,000+ warehouses, 40+ owned vehicles, 1,300+ installation partners.
demand_pricing: Order book stands at INR 788 crore, covering orders as of 30 September 2026 plus orders received from 1 October 2026.
Cumulative FY27 orders of INR 1,422.29 crore incl. GST, excluding the BESS order. Management said close to INR 900 crore of the order book has already been executed.
Management said it needs about INR 500 crore of fresh orders to reach its INR 2,200 crore revenue scenario without PM KUSUM.
Pump receivables described as a pan-India average tied to government scheme payments after survey, installation, inspection; farmers pay their share upfront.
Rooftop is cash-and-carry per management, with margins targeted slightly below pumps.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 1,800 crore is revenue visibility covering the current year's order book plus opening order book; close to INR 900 crore has already been executed.

qa_highlights.question: How can FY27 margins hold at 17-18% given Q1 about 16% and Q2 about 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it intends to maintain the 17-18% range, citing planning and a controlled manufacturing ecosystem, and is confident it will do so.

qa_highlights.question: What drives 35-40% growth if PM KUSUM is delayed, and how does it square with the INR 788 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the existing pump orders, retail rooftop, and Magel Tyala 7 pipeline; it said about INR 500 crore of new orders must be secured to reach INR 2,200 crore total.

qa_highlights.question: What are rooftop margins and working capital needs for the large rooftop order?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are expected slightly lower than pumps; total cash cycle is 45-60 days in rooftop.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and reason for PM KUSUM 2.0 delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied a delay, saying it had guided to Q3 announcement and benefits from Q4 onwards; technical discussions on product upgrades are ongoing with management's input.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be fresh equity or more borrowing to fund working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no fresh equity plan at current prices; promoters at about 79% would dilute to 75% in about two years if needed; debt raised so far is considered sufficient.

544527|2026-09.headline: Atlanta Electricals Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23.1% YoY to INR390.1 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 15.3% on firm-price contracts and ~INR180 crore of deferred deliveries.
544527|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 23.1% YoY to INR390.1 crore, while gross margin fell to 26.6% from 30.9% and EBITDA margin to 15.3% from 17.3%. Management attributed the squeeze to elevated transformer oil, copper and steel prices on firm-price orders (about 15% of quarterly revenue) and Gujarat monsoon disruptions that delayed customer acceptance of finished transformers worth about INR180 crore. PAT rose 28% YoY to INR32.1 crore, helped by lower finance costs. Order book reached INR3,197 crore, up 54.5% YoY, but Q2 order inflow was only about INR421 crore as management chose to limit 220 kV and below bookings.

segments.name: Transformers - 220 kV and below (current book)
segments.commentary: About 47% of the order book is 220 kV class per management. Management said it deliberately limited new 220 kV and below bookings in Q2 given a large Q1 booking base.

segments.name: Transformers - 400 kV class
segments.commentary: About 8.6% of the order book is 400 kV class (INR184 crore per management). First 315 MVA, 400 kV unit commenced manufacturing on 26 Oct 2026; commercial contribution targeted in Q4 FY27 after testing.

segments.commentary: First US order for a special duty transformer, for a new US transformer plant. US inquiries of about 120 transformers (9,300 MVA). Medium-term aspiration of exports at about 15% of revenue within 2 years.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin for FY27 and FY28 expected in the 16% to 18% range; management said it remains firm on achieving this in both years.
3-year revenue growth aspiration of approximately 40% CAGR reiterated; CEO-level comment that 40% is a minimum, and management said FY28 is covered but would not give FY29 guidance.
About 70% of the INR180 crore deferred orders already dispatched in October; remainder expected in Q3 FY27, subject to customer site readiness.
Remaining firm-price orders (about 10-12% of order book per CFO, 3-4% per COO) expected to be substantially executed in Q3 FY27, with price revisions reportedly obtained from customers.
Management expects H2 to be stronger than H1 seasonally and expects margin correction in Q3 and Q4; target utilisation of 80%.
capex_capacity: Dedicated inverter duty transformer (IDT) plant: about 5,000 MVA capacity, capex INR65 crore, civil work complete, commissioning expected before end-Q3 FY27; 33 kV IDT production moves from Unit 2 to free Unit 2 for 66 and 132 kV classes.

Tank and radiator backward integration via AE Components: capex about INR193 crore (INR196 crore cited later in Q&A, likely the same project), groundbreaking done, commissioning targeted October 2027. Funded mainly through internal accruals, with term loans tied up but undrawn as a backup.
Utilisation as stated in Q&A: Unit 1 at 60%, Unit 2 at 40%, Bangalore at about 90%, Vadod at about 30%, Jambusar (765 kV plant) at about 7-8%.

765 kV: in-house design of first 765 kV reactor started; production targeted in Q4 FY27 with completion and testing between Q4 FY27 and Q1 FY28. International technology partnership not progressed due to sanctions constraints; management says partnership remains open.
Vadod facility has approvals from NTPC Solar, NTPC Renewables, Tata Power, KPTCL and Punjab Transmission Company.
demand_pricing: Order book INR3,196.97 crore at 30 Sep 2026, vs INR3,116.63 crore at end-June and about INR2,069 crore a year ago (+54.5% YoY).
Q2 order inflow about INR421 crore; management called the slowdown a deliberate decision to limit 220 kV and below orders, and cited commodity volatility delaying some L1 tenders.
Inquiry pipeline about INR19,464 crore. Battery energy storage pipeline of about 3,400 MVA worth INR184 crore.

Pricing: majority of orders carry price variation clauses. Since the Middle East conflict began in March 2026, new quotes are mostly on price-variation basis; management said no pressure yet seen on pricing or inquiry pipeline.
LOI worth INR193.92 crore from APTRANSCO for 12 units of 160 MVA, 220 kV class autotransformers. 12 new customers added in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 765 kV plant ramp-up delayed by the lack of a technology partner, and will the designs align with Power Grid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the partner route remains open but it is proceeding in-house; 765 kV is in Unit 5 and 400 kV in Unit 4 in parallel. COO said CEA has standardised 400 and 765 kV specifications, so designs are acceptable to Power Grid and other Indian customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did order inflow fall about 55% QoQ, and what to expect in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO-level answer: a management decision to cautiously book 220 kV and below orders after a large Q1 booking base covering about 1.5 years; 400 kV and above will be the focus once a 400 kV prototype is ready. Management said the INR3,000 crore-plus book covers visibility.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is firm-price, and will new orders carry price variation clauses?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said firm-price share is 10-12%; COO later said 3-4%. COO said new quotes since March are price-variation based, with at most 1-2% of the last six months' book on firm price.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR193 crore capex be funded, and is more capex planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Funded mainly from internal accruals, with bank term loans tied up but not drawn. No other major capex planned beyond small staff housing projects.

qa_highlights.question: Will the remaining firm-price orders keep margins down in Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: COO said customers agreed to price revisions bringing 2025 booking prices in line with current levels, so no major negative margin impact is expected in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margins reach the earlier 18-19% aspiration, and what is the pricing outlook from new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO reiterated the 16-18% FY27-FY28 range, with H2 expected to lift margins through operating leverage. COO said no pricing pressure seen so far, though some peers are expanding capacity.

risks_watch: Gross margin compression on remaining firm-price orders and commodity volatility (transformer oil, copper, steel) that management says is still a key factor to monitor.
Customer site readiness: about 30% of the INR180 crore deferred orders is still pending dispatch, with completion targeted in Q3 FY27.
Inventory rose to INR632.9 crore from INR364.1 crore in six months, creating working capital pressure. Management expects it to unwind as deferred orders are executed.
Supply chain risk for critical components (bushings, containers) due to typhoons and Middle East conflict; management says the issue is temporary.
Execution risk on 400 kV first unit (commercial contribution Q4 FY27) and 765 kV production (Q4 FY27), with the technology partner route stalled by sanctions.
Order inflow slowdown in Q2 and the low utilisation of Vadod (30%) and Jambusar (7-8%) plants; the IDT and backward integration commissioning dates are key checkpoints.
544527|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook and margin range, but defensive about the Q2 miss, attributing it to weather, commodity costs and deferred deliveries. Management was evasive on FY29 targets and US margin uplift, and gave inconsistent answers on firm-price order share (10-12% vs 3-4%).
key_quotes: Importantly, these represent deferred deliveries and not cancellations and these orders continue to remain part of our order book.
We maintain that our EBITDA margin for FY27 and FY28 would be ranging around 16% to 18%, and we are still firm on the belief that we will be achieving this margin in current year and coming year.
Green Energy Corridors will definitely improve the demand, but, on our side, we will still try and at least commit 40%.

544528|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20.3% QoQ to INR2,267 million but fell 5% YoY on West Bengal atta disruption; EBITDA margin 13%.
544528|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations was INR2,267 million, up 20.3% QoQ and down 5% YoY, with B2C down 2.5% YoY almost entirely due to atta. Excluding atta, B2C grew 4.9% YoY and 26% QoQ. Operating EBITDA rose 23.6% YoY to INR295 million at a 13% margin (+302 bps YoY), helped mainly by lower other expenses from advertising phasing. PAT rose 68.7% YoY to INR188 million as finance costs fell to INR6 million. Management guided FY27 revenue down about 5% and EBITDA margin up 50-70 bps, with H2 margins structurally lower than H1.

544529|2026-09.headline: Aptus Pharma H1 FY27 revenue rose to Rs 48.90 crore from Rs 14.38 crore, with PAT of about Rs 5.08 crore; no forward guidance given.
544529|2026-09.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 (half-year ended 30 September 2026) revenue from operations of about Rs 48.90 crore versus Rs 14.38 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of about Rs 7.68 crore, PBT of about Rs 6.83 crore and PAT of about Rs 5.08 crore. Management stressed working capital discipline, with inventory of about Rs 16.25 crore and trade receivables of about Rs 28.64 crore against total assets of about Rs 54.55 crore. The strategy was reiterated as three pillars: manufacturing (about 20% of portfolio self-made by March 2028), pan-India expansion (46% geographic coverage by March 2027, pan-India by 2029) and international expansion. Management declined to give any quantitative guidance on revenue, EBITDA, PAT or capex returns during the Q&A.

544530|2026-03.headline: Anand Rathi Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 125.7% YoY to ₹416 million on revenue of ₹2,557 million, while the MTF book fell 10.53% QoQ.
544530|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 28.1% YoY to ₹2,557 million, with EBITDA up 51.4% to ₹1,103 million (43.2% margin) and PAT up 125.7% to ₹416 million. Full-year FY26 revenue grew 10.2% to ₹9,322 million, EBITDA rose 21.9% to ₹3,796 million, and PAT rose 24.8% to ₹1,293 million. Non-broking income (MTF interest, distribution, other) rose to 53% of the mix in Q4 and 49% for the year, while the MTF book declined from ₹12,317 million in December 2025 to ₹11,019 million in March 2026 due to RBI funding-policy changes and weak markets. Management proposed a ₹5 per share dividend.

segments.name: Broking and related services
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue ₹1,201 million (+14.5% YoY); FY26 ₹4,755 million (-6.8% YoY). FY26 mix: equity cash 51%, F&O 41%, other 8%; Q4 mix: 49%, 41%, 10%.

segments.name: Non-broking (MTF, distribution, other)
segments.commentary: MTF book ₹11,019 million with zero NPA and ~61% of exposure from clients with balances below ₹1 crore. Distribution income rose 44.1% in FY26 to ₹1,129 million, spanning MF, PMS, AIF, insurance, bonds, structured products and FDs.

segments.name: Asset management / custody
segments.commentary: AUM ₹77,876 million (+21% YoY); assets under custody ₹944,155 million (+16% YoY). Insurance corporate agency licence obtained in FY26; life and health insurance distribution has started.

guidance_outlook: Target revenue mix of 50:50 between broking and non-broking, with both growing steadily; management said it is not yet happy with the current 51:49 split and expects to reach 50:50 over time.
Management expects non-broking to grow about 40-45% annually for the first few years, and broking about 15% a year.
Overall revenue growth aim of about 15-20% YoY.
Earlier guidance of an MTF book of ₹15,000 million by FY26 was missed; the book ended at ₹11,019 million.
Debt-equity ceiling set at a maximum of 1.5x; current ratio is about 0.6x.
capex_capacity: MTF book contracted 10.53% QoQ in Q4 FY26 after RBI policy changes narrowed bank and NBFC funding avenues for capital market intermediaries; management said the company had to control growth and preserve cash for margin requirements.
Management said the RBI funding-related deferral was postponed to another quarter, and expects to resume MTF growth as funding routes reopen.
IPO completed in September 2025 raising ₹745 crore, used mainly for working capital.
Stock basket for MTF restricted internally to fewer than 1,000 stocks versus about 2,000+ permitted by the regulator; internal margins set above exchange margins for many stocks.
Branch network and business partner expansion planned in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets.
demand_pricing: Market backdrop: Nifty fell about 15% in Q4 FY26 and the company described a consolidation phase, FII outflows and West Asia-related volatility; clients became cautious on new and existing positions.
Demat accounts rose from 15.14 crore (Mar 2024) to 22.2 crore (Feb 2026); mutual fund AUM about ₹82.02 lakh crore (Feb 2026), up 24.8% YoY.
Active client base was flat to down 2-3% in FY26, while total client base grew 12.7% (corrected from 12%).
MTF yields: management said no significant pricing pressure yet despite competitor entry, with low MTF penetration among its clients; it did not rule out yield changes.
About 42% of active clients have been with the company for over five years; 83% of active clients are over 30 years old; about 60% of broking clients use the digital platform.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company guide broking and wealth management over coming quarters (client acquisition, advisory, digital)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wealth management sits in a separate group company; this entity focuses on broking and distribution, with a phygital model and about 60% of broking clients on the digital platform.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company manage risks in broking and advisory (volatility, compliance, credit) while keeping profitability stable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited restricting the MTF basket to under 1,000 stocks, higher-than-exchange margins, zero MTF NPA over eight-plus years, QSB broker status and a debt-equity ceiling of 1.5x.

qa_highlights.question: How should the 50:50 broking/non-broking mix evolve over the next couple of years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects non-broking to grow 40-45% a year and broking about 15%, with overall revenue growth of 15-20% a year.

qa_highlights.question: Are MTF spreads sustainable amid new competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not facing much pressure yet due to pent-up demand and low utilisation; yields may change but it aims to maintain current levels, with growth gated by capital and funding.

qa_highlights.question: How much of broking is derivatives vs cash, and what is the STT impact? What is exposure to the RBI proprietary-trading rule?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue split is about 50:50 cash vs derivatives, with focus on hedged and investment-led F&O and commodity trades. The company said it has no proprietary book, so the RBI prop-book rule does not affect it. The STT impact was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: How much of AUC growth came from new clients vs existing clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AUC growth came mainly from existing clients, with the total client base up 12.7% and active clients flat to down 2-3% in FY26.

risks_watch: MTF book contraction (down 10.53% QoQ) and dependence on bank/NBFC funding under RBI rules; watch the funding reopening and the ₹15,000 million target.
Broking revenue fell 6.8% in FY26 with active clients flat to down, and F&O is 41% of the mix; the sensitivity to market cycles and STT changes is not quantified.
Competition in MTF could pressure yields; management said it is not yet seeing it.
Q4 PAT (+125.7%) may not be a clean run-rate given the quarterly volatility; watch whether margins hold when markets are weak.
Growth in non-broking (40-45%) and broking (~15%) is aspirational, given FY26 broking was down.

544530|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.37% YoY to ₹2,461 million, but PAT after a ₹209.96 million exceptional fraud charge was ₹233.51 million (+2.35% YoY).
544530|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 22.37% YoY to about ₹2,461 million, with EBITDA up 30.19% to ₹973 million at a 39.54% margin. PAT before exceptional items rose about 71% to ₹391 million, but a ₹209.96 million exceptional charge for restoring securities to two dormant depository clients cut reported PAT to ₹233.51 million. MTF book reached ₹13,318 million (+55% YoY) and distribution AUM ₹94,791 million (+25.82% YoY). Management guided MTF to ₹1,750–1,800 crores and distribution AUM up 40% by year-end FY27.

segments.name: Broking
segments.commentary: Contributed 52% of revenue; broking income ₹1,280 million, up about 7% QoQ, with 51% of it from equity cash, the core focus area.

segments.name: Non-broking (MTF + distribution)
segments.commentary: Contributed 29% of revenue; MTF interest income ₹428 million and distribution income ₹275 million. Distribution income dipped QoQ, which management attributed to seasonally lower insurance sales in April–June.

segments.name: Employees
segments.commentary: Headcount 2,263 versus 2,148 in Q1 FY26.

guidance_outlook: MTF book expected at ₹1,750–1,800 crores by end of FY27, from ₹1,330 crores currently.
Distribution AUM targeted to grow about 40%, driven by higher wallet share of existing clients.
Continue to target a near 50:50 broking to non-broking income mix over the medium term.
Long-term revenue growth band of 15–25% (typically 20–25%); PAT growth target of around 30–35% while the mix is not yet 50:50.
Planned Dubai subsidiary to serve UAE-based NRI clients, subject to licences; board has passed a resolution.
Management expects borrowings to rise to lift the debt-equity ratio, which it sees as comfortable at around 2x versus industry 1.5–2x.
capex_capacity: MTF book rose from about ₹1,100 crores at the March 2026 trough to ₹1,330 crores, with growth continuing in Q1.
Management said borrowing is being used to fund working capital and MTF; it expects leverage to rise from 0.81x.
Credit rating upgraded: short-term bank facilities to A1+, long-term to A+.
Dubai subsidiary planned for NRI servicing; a GIFT City subsidiary already exists and is active for NRI business.
demand_pricing: Cash market turnover rose about 13% QoQ, while derivatives activity moderated after SEBI measures (upfront option premium, expiry-day margins, higher contract sizes, weekly expiry rationalisation).
RBI revised capital market exposure framework effective 1 July 2026 is expected to raise bank working-capital costs for broking intermediaries.
MTF yield about 14%; management said spreads depend on market liquidity and borrowing costs, which are currently higher.
Demat accounts reached 23 crore in June; SIP additions about 66 lakh in June versus 53 lakh in March; 42 companies filed draft offer documents with SEBI in the quarter.

Distribution revenue in April–June fell QoQ because insurance sales are concentrated in January–March; mutual fund and other AUM grew QoQ and the company recorded its highest net collections in the last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was MTF interest income flat despite about 21% book growth, and is MTF pricing falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Average MTF book was flat QoQ because it fell to about ₹1,100 crores in March after a mid-cap sell-off of about 15%, then recovered to ₹1,330 crores by quarter end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MTF risk management approach?
qa_highlights.answer: MTF is funded only against cash-market securities chosen from a restricted list, with no F&O allocation, per-customer and per-scrip limits, and a book mostly below ₹1 crore per client. Management said there have been no delinquencies since 2017.

qa_highlights.question: What was the fraud, and what has been done to prevent recurrence?
qa_highlights.answer: Two dormant depository clients lost securities through fraudulent off-market transfers noticed about a year later. The company replenished the securities, filed an FIR with EOW (assets frozen), lodged an insurance claim, appointed EY for forensic audit and hired an external consultant. Recoveries will be booked only when reasonably certain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue growth guidance given the 22% Q1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for 20–25% growth, within a 15–25% range, with PAT growth of 30–35%, until the 50:50 broking and non-broking mix is reached.

qa_highlights.question: Why did non-broking decline QoQ and how will this be avoided?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said distribution is seasonal, with insurance sales concentrated in January–March; the April–June fall was driven by insurance, while other products grew. Trail revenue was also hit by the March market fall.

qa_highlights.question: Why is debt-equity elevated and will leverage increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-equity fell after the IPO equity infusion; management intends to borrow more to fund MTF and working capital, saying 1.5–2x is comfortable for the industry, versus 0.81x now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MTF yield and the sustainability of spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: MTF yield is about 14%. Management said spreads depend on liquidity, with borrowing costs currently higher, and that higher costs can be passed to clients.

risks_watch: ₹209.96 million exceptional fraud charge; recovery depends on insurance claim settlement and frozen assets, with timing uncertain. External forensic audit still in progress.
RBI capital market exposure framework from 1 July 2026 may raise bank borrowing costs and working-capital needs for brokers.
MTF book (₹13,318 million) is sensitive to market sell-offs, as the March 2026 trough showed; leverage is planned to rise from 0.81x.
Derivatives activity is moderating under SEBI curbs, and distribution revenue is seasonal.
Dubai subsidiary licensing and GIFT City international offering are still early-stage.

544530|2026-09.headline: Anand Rathi Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR2,732 million and PAT rose 50% to INR419 million, a record quarter per management.

H1 revenue rose 21% to INR5,193 million; H1 PAT after exceptional items was INR653 million (up 29%), and PAT before exceptional items was INR810 million (up 60%). Broking and related services grew 34% YoY to INR1,551 million, while the MTF book reached INR14,993 million at 30 September, already about 57% of the year-end guidance. Management said market volumes were weak in derivatives but cash volumes were improving, and it discussed the drop in net cash, which it attributed to clients moving margins from FDs into G-Secs.

544531|2026-09.headline: True Colors H1 FY27 revenue rose 21.1% to INR 183.01 crore, with PAT up 43.3% to INR 21.09 crore as consumables drove margins.
544531|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations grew 21.1% YoY to INR 183.01 crore, and profit grew roughly twice as fast, with EBITDA up 40.1% to INR 32.34 crore and EBITDA margin up 240 bps to 17.7%. Management attributed the margin gain to a richer mix of ink and paper, which made up 56.2% of revenue versus 48.7% a year earlier. Operating cash flow turned positive at INR 27.16 crore against an outflow of INR 10.90 crore last year. Management announced a 50:50 JV with Swastik Strategic Ventures LLP for a pulp-to-coated-paper plant at Bardoli (INR 320-340 crore) and began in-house ink production plans under INKIA.

544532|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 235% YoY to INR591 crore, but EBITDA margin was 12.1% and FY26 PAT margin 8.5%, below the 11% promised earlier.
544532|2026-03.overview: Solarworld reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations of INR591 crore (up 235% YoY), EBITDA of INR73 crore (12.1% margin) and PAT of INR49 crore (8.1% net margin). For FY26, total income was INR1,416 crore (up 1.57% YoY), EBITDA INR187.9 crore (13.3%) and PAT INR120.4 crore (8.5%). Management blamed a loss-making initial module ramp after ALMM approval in December 2025 and sharp raw material cost increases in Q4 linked to the West Asia conflict. The company is pivoting toward BESS, with a 582 MWac / 1.2 GWh DC BESS project pipeline and a 3.4 GW BESS line in trials.

Ethanol allocations were increased during the quarter after a Supreme Court judgment, lifting the last supply year's allocation from 24.5 crore litres to 34.5 crore litres, with a further 5 crore litres reported. segments.name: SAF (sustainable aviation fuel)
segments.commentary: Front-end engineering is ongoing and about INR150 crore of viability gap funding has been received under PM JI-VAN for the proposed plant. Capex awaits a government roadmap that has not yet been announced.

544546|2026-03.overview: Chatterbox Technologies held its maiden earnings call for FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026), its first since its IPO. Margins moderated, which management attributed to investment in talent, platform capabilities and new verticals. Management declined to give formal guidance, though it said FY27 net margins would be similar to FY26 with an aim to expand them. segments.commentary: Contributed 36.18% of FY26 revenue. No separate growth or margin commentary was given in the call.

segments.name: ChtrSocial
segments.commentary: Contributed 24.55% of FY26 revenue. Management called it one of the fastest-growing verticals and among the highest-margin, and said it expects revenue to at least double in the coming period, without giving a percentage target.

segments.name: International (Chtr International / Dubai subsidiary)
segments.commentary: About 18% of FY26 revenue. Dubai subsidiary is the gateway to the Middle East; priority markets are MENA, with APAC and LATAM evaluated selectively. Management said it will expand in a lean way.

capex_capacity: Intangible assets roughly doubled, while intangible assets under development stayed at INR4.68 crores; the AAGE app was on hold during the IPO and is being resumed.

544547|2026-03.headline: Jinkushal Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 89% YoY to INR133 crore, a record quarter, but full-year PAT was only INR12.44 crore as logistics and HexL brand costs weighed.

544550|2026-03.headline: Pace Digitek Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 60.5% YoY to Rs.1,097 crore; FY26 PAT Rs.307 crore (+10.1%), FY27 revenue guided Rs.3,200-3,400 crore.
544550|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was Rs.1,097 crore versus Rs.683 crore a year earlier, driven by project execution. Full-year revenue grew 8.3% to Rs.2,641 crore and PAT rose 10.1% to Rs.307 crore, but full-year EBITDA fell to Rs.455 crore from Rs.482 crore as the mix shifted from telecom to energy. Working capital absorbed cash: inventory was built to Rs.540 crore and trade receivables reached Rs.2,442 crore, which management expects to ease by September 2026. BESS manufacturing capacity is being raised from 2.5 GWh to 5 GWh (July 2026) and 10 GWh (October 2026).

Management said competition will rise; the company claims about 6 GWh open order book and first commissioned project (September 2025) as operating credential.

qa_highlights.question: Is the capacity commissioning delay a bottleneck, and are imports from China affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the delay was two months, caused by West Asia shipping disruption; equipment has arrived and will be commissioned in June and operational from July 2026.

qa_highlights.answer: Container realisation is about $82-84/kWh and cell cost $48-50/kWh (60-65% of container cost); management expects prices to ease from the next quarter and is not delaying projects currently.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 margins hold given energy is the bulk of the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Energy EBITDA margins are lower than telecom; PAT margin is expected to be 10-11% in FY27 versus 11.4% in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why do FY25 receivables differ from the RHP figures?

qa_highlights.question: Why was working capital stretched and when will it normalise?
