544550|2026-06.headline: Pace Digitek Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 51.3% YoY to Rs.555 crore; FY27 guidance of Rs.3,200-3,400 crore reiterated on Rs.10,803 crore executable order book.
544550|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs.555 crore (up 51.3% YoY) but down sharply from Rs.1,097 crore in Q4 FY26, which management attributed to milestone-based recognition and a high Q4 base. EBITDA was Rs.86.1 crore (15.5% margin vs 14.9% in Q4) and PAT was Rs.63 crore (11.3% margin vs Rs.55 crore in Q1 FY26). Order inflow in the quarter was about Rs.1,677 crore, with two energy EPC wins (NLC, DVC, ~Rs.1,412 crore) and a BSNL OFC project (~Rs.265 crore). Management said the 5 GWh BESS line is operational, with a further 5 GWh line due to be commissioned by December 2026, and reiterated the FY27 revenue guidance.

segments.name: Energy (BESS, renewable EPC, BOO)
segments.commentary: Contributed 79.5% of Q1 revenue and is the main growth driver; energy executable order book Rs.8,453 crore, split Rs.4,074 crore BOO and Rs.4,367 crore EPC. Management expects energy to be about 65-70% of the order book by year end.

segments.name: Telecom & ICT (BharatNet, Railway Kavach, BSNL OFC)
segments.commentary: Contributed 20.5% of Q1 revenue; executable order book Rs.2,350 crore. Kavach about 30% complete; BSNL OFC (~Rs.265 crore) to execute over about 2.5 years. Management said telecom has better margins but lower volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of Rs.3,200-3,400 crore reiterated; management said it sees no concern in achieving it, with most revenue expected from the existing order book.
H1 FY27 targeted at 40-45% of full-year revenue vs 35% in H1 FY26.
Q2 container supply planned at 210 units; management expects about 125+ containers per month in the next calendar year.
FY27 PAT margin guidance of 10.5-11% for BESS, with the lithium-ion cell cost increase said to be factored in.
Cash flow from operations expected to turn positive by March 2027; inventory and receivables expected to stabilise between December and March.
Energy-to-telecom order book mix expected to move to about 65:35 or 70:30 by year end.
capex_capacity: BESS capacity is 5 GWh operational (two 2.5 GWh lines); a third 5 GWh line is due for installation in October 2026, targeting 10 GWh by early December 2026 as India's largest operational BESS facility.
Total capex of about Rs.300 crore for the 5 GWh expansion phase, the container fabrication unit, and related setup, mainly land cost, funded from the earlier private placement.
In-house container manufacturing started with trials this month; batch production from next month. Over 300 containers supplied to date.

BOO projects: 975 MWh commissioned to date (MSEDCL standalone BESS, about Rs.900 crore recognised in P&L); four BOO projects expected to add about Rs.750 crore annual revenue once all are commissioned.
Pune R&D centre inaugurated about three weeks ago; cell manufacturing planning under way. Applying for 4 GWh under the government cell PLI scheme (10 GWh total scheme).
demand_pricing: Bidding for about 27 GWh of tenders; NTPC Renewable Energy and NTPC Green tenders noted, with NTPC Green tenders drawing only 7-8 bidders versus 32-51 in earlier state tenders.
Management said bidding aggression has eased after a 4 GWh Maharashtra project was cancelled and a Punjab tender saw a single bid at higher prices.
Management said cell cost is about 60% of total BESS cost, unchanged; recent tenders include price variation clauses while older tenders do not. Stock was built in March to lower Q1 cell costs.

C&I BESS (below 5 MWh) received product approval from large Indian customers; first trial order of about 25 units, with management referring to potential for thousands per year. Management guided C&I EBITDA margin about 4-5 points above grid-scale product margin of 13-15%.
Container unit value about Rs.4-4.5 crore; about 70 containers per month currently.
Early exports: small container supply to a Saudi company in Q1 and an MoU signed in Saudi Arabia.
MEGMEET tie-up for AI data-centre power solutions in India; demo equipment planned; management said a concrete revenue plan could come in about one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Telecom & ICT order inflow break-up and execution timeline for the Rs.2,350 crore telecom book?
qa_highlights.answer: Of Rs.1,677 crore inflow, NLC and DVC EPC wins were about Rs.1,412 crore and BSNL OFC about Rs.265 crore. EPC projects run about one year; OFC about 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 guidance not higher given the energy order book visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: BOO solar-plus-BESS capex is capitalised as a fixed asset and not recognised as revenue, so physical execution will exceed reported revenue. Revenue recognition comes from EPC and standalone BESS in BOO.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash flow and working-capital profile by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Telecom net working capital is about 5 months (~150 days); energy is expected at 90-100 days. Management expects operating cash flow to turn positive by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue path needed from Q2 onwards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most of the remaining Rs.2,700 crore should come from the existing order book, with Q1 seasonally low due to government funding and approval cycles.

qa_highlights.question: How will rising lithium-ion cell prices affect EPC and BOO margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of 10.5-11% margin already includes anticipated cell price increases; price variation clauses in new tenders and stock built in March mitigate impact.

544550|2026-09.headline: Pace Digitek Q2 FY27 revenue rose 51.5% YoY to Rs 808 crore and FY27 revenue guidance was raised to Rs 3,300-3,500 crore.
544550|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 808 crore (+51.5% YoY, +45.5% QoQ) and H1 revenue was Rs 1,364 crore (+51.4%), with energy about 80% and telecom about 20%. Q2 EBITDA rose 68.5% YoY to Rs 159 crore and PAT rose 43.3% to Rs 97 crore, though management said margins were flattered by a higher telecom services mix. Borrowings rose to Rs 1,371 crore from Rs 961 crore in March 2026, driven by build-to-operate (BOT) assets, and net debt-to-equity moved to 0.35x. Management raised FY27 revenue guidance but kept FY28 at Rs 4,000-4,200 crore, and said it has paused new BOT projects without external investment.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 28 crore in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.value: Rs 10,735 crore (energy Rs 8,528 crore; telecom Rs 2,208 crore)
financial_highlights.change: H1 inflows Rs 2,437 crore (energy Rs 2,173 crore; telecom Rs 265 crore)

segments.name: Energy (BESS)
segments.commentary: Energy contributed about 80% of H1 revenue; energy EBITDA margin is 12-13% per management, and the combined EBITDA margin was flattered by telecom services. H1 BESS commissioning was about 875 MWh, with 1.8 GWh delivered to customers to date.

segments.name: Telecom
segments.commentary: Telecom contributed about 20% of revenue, with EBITDA margin around 20% (20-23% on projects, about 25% on O&M). More than 8,000 BSNL sites were commissioned and entered a 5-year O&M phase.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance raised to Rs 3,300-3,500 crore from Rs 3,200-3,400 crore.
FY28 revenue guidance unchanged at Rs 4,000-4,200 crore; management said it sees 'a much better guidance' than provided but has not revised it.
FY28 PAT margin guided at about 10% (management later said 10-11%), down from the 11-12% level seen in H1 FY27, which was helped by telecom turnkey projects.
Blended EBITDA margin expected at 16-17% as energy mix rises; container in-house fabrication expected to cut BESS cost by 4-5% gross and add about 1.5-2% at EBITDA level.
Build-to-operate revenue expected at Rs 325-375 crore in FY28, after Rs 197 crore from the current project and about Rs 200 crore from two projects commissioning by March 2027.
Peak debt expected at around Rs 1,100 crore of additional borrowing by March 2027, with about Rs 1,600 crore of back-to-back BOT assets.
C&I to target about 30% of energy revenue in the next financial year (FY28); C&I margins expected to lift blended EBITDA by at least 1-2%.
capex_capacity: BESS manufacturing capacity expanded from 2.5 GWh to 5 GWh in August 2026; production currently running at full 5 GWh. About 844 MWh produced in H1 FY27, equal to 94% of FY26 output.
Expansion to 10 GWh: an additional 5 GWh setup to be completed in Q3 FY27, with production starting in Q4 and about one quarter needed to reach full utilisation.
In-house BESS container facility: trial production from November 2026 and full-scale production from January 2027, expected to meet about 50% of container requirements.
BESS volume target of about 200 containers per quarter; Q2 sold about 91 containers plus 10 in stock (about 100), and Q3 target is slightly below 200.

Build-to-operate asset stood at Rs 1,311 crore at 30 Sep 2026; about 60% commissioned, with completion expected December 2026 or January 2027. Management has paused new BOT projects absent external investment.
4 GWh cell manufacturing (PLI) tendering expected to complete by mid-November 2026; cell plant to start in the next financial year, with technology transfer still under study at the R&D centre.
demand_pricing: Management sees BESS demand of about 30-35 GWh in FY27, rising to about 236 GWh by FY32.
Bidding competition has eased: about 6-8 participants per tender now versus 25-30 earlier; management said margin pressure persists but is smaller.
Lithium-ion cell prices rose about 20% in the prior quarter, hurting energy project margins; prices are now falling and expected to stabilise. Tenders bid over the last 3-4 months use the new prices.
Landed Chinese BESS price is roughly in line with Pace's manufacturing cost plus margin.
From January 2027, about 6% export rebate cut on Chinese cell imports; management expects lower cell prices to offset it.
Standalone EBITDA margin fell due to early-stage MAHAGENCO solar supply-and-erection and Bondada balance-of-systems projects with higher initial mobilisation costs.
Receivable days were about 286 at March 2026; management expects receivable cycle near 150 days and payables of 60-90 days, for a net working capital cycle of 90-120 days.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp EBITDA margin improvement and how should margins trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets 17-19% EBITDA margin and that H1 was lifted by a larger telecom services share; energy margins are 12-13% and telecom about 20%. Blended margin is expected to fall to 16-17% as energy grows.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 container volumes and Q3-Q4 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About 100 containers in Q2 (91 sold, 10 stocked) on an unchanged 2.5 GWh base, because the expanded capacity only started commercial production in September. Q3 is targeted at slightly below 200 containers.

qa_highlights.question: Benefit from in-house container fabrication?
qa_highlights.answer: Container cost expected to fall about 25%, BESS overall cost 4-5% at gross level, and about 1.5-2% at EBITDA level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Q2 standalone and energy margins decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Two new solar projects (MAHAGENCO and Bondada) carry high initial mobilisation costs, plus a 20% rise in lithium-ion cell prices last quarter and early-stage costs at the new BESS capacity. Management expects a slight recovery in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10 GWh capacity supported by enough BESS demand, and how is FY28 guidance framed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand of 30-35 GWh in FY27 and 236 GWh by FY32 supports capacity; the 10 GWh is to reach full utilisation one quarter after Q4 start. FY28 guidance was not revised but management expects better. Revenue realisation is spread over about 2 years because most product goes into EPC and BOT projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working-capital outlook for receivables and payables?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables are falling as telecom retentions are collected, and management expects receivable days near 150 and payables of 60-90 days. Consolidated payables fell from about Rs 1,800 crore to Rs 1,500 crore, with a target of Rs 800-900 crore.

Lithium-ion cell price volatility and the January 2027 export rebate cut on Chinese cells; the technology-transfer timeline for cells is still unclear.

544558|2026-03.headline: Fabtech FY26 total income rose 28.4% to ₹431.33 crore, but margins compressed; management guides ~25% growth and 9.9–10.5% PAT margin.
544558|2026-03.overview: FY26 total income grew 28.4% YoY to ₹431.33 crore and EBITDA rose 18.29% to ₹55.56 crore, while reported net profit fell to ₹38.36 crore from ₹46.45 crore (FY25 included ₹17.85 crore exceptional item). Q4 total income rose 22% YoY to ₹168.24 crore and quarterly net profit rebounded to ₹22.06 crore. Margin pressure was attributed to remobilisation, a 33% rise in RMC cost and a 43% rise in execution cost, amid Middle East disruption. Cash and bank balance rose to ₹208.57 crore after a ~₹230 crore equity infusion (IPO), while receivables rose to ₹204.34 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Middle East conflict on Q4 and expected impact going forward?

UAE FTS faced war-related headwinds, and several large orders slipped (not cancelled) into later quarters. Management reiterated 20-25% organic growth for FY27, with Q2 steady and Q3-Q4 stronger, and guided PAT margin of 9-11%.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said on-site teams kept executing, but conversions slowed as customers delayed decisions. Management said working capital has not been impacted much, and the company is using outsourced labour selectively.

qa_highlights.answer: Management is reworking contracts with auditors to define billable milestones tied to percentage completion. Existing contracts stay on shipment/milestone basis, and changes are expected over the next few years.

544563|2026-03.headline: Zelio FY26 consolidated revenue rose 81.8% to INR313 crore, EBITDA INR38.01 crore at 12.2% margin, PAT INR28.39 crore; FY27 target 125,000 units.
544563|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 (year ended March 31, 2026) consolidated revenue from operations of INR310.71 crore (total revenue INR313.68 crore), up 81.8%, with EBITDA of INR38.01 crore and PAT of INR28.39 crore. Two-wheeler volumes reached more than 70,000 units (H1 30,000, H2 40,000+), and capacity was expanded from 72,000 to 240,000 units across four plants. Management guided to 75-80% revenue growth and more than 125,000 units in FY27, with Coimbatore (Tamil Nadu) and Patan (Haryana, three-wheelers) commissioned in July 2026 per the script. The call was largely Q&A on volumes, dealers, financing, capex and governance; many answers were qualitative or repeated the same targets.

segments.name: Two-wheelers (low-speed EV scooters)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume above 70,000 units, with H2 above H1 (40,000+ vs 30,000). Average selling price cited at about INR44,000, with management expecting INR45,000-50,000 over time.

segments.name: Three-wheelers
segments.commentary: FY26 volume of only 800 units because plant was not ready. FY27 target is more than 2,000 units, with production from the Patan, Haryana plant.

segments.name: Zelio Auto Components (wholly-owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Incorporated to control component procurement and spare parts supply; management says it is already contributing positively to consolidated revenue and profitability. No separate figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target of more than 125,000 units.
Revenue growth target of 75-80% YoY, described as a repeatable structural trajectory.
Dealer network to expand from more than 400 to more than 550 in FY27 (100-150 new dealers); 100% of dealerships to be exclusive by this year.
Three-wheeler FY27 target of more than 2,000 units.

Management said EBITDA and PAT margins will be maintained despite higher branding and promotion spend; marketing spend for FY27 not yet decided, with FY26 non-IPL promotional spend stated as more than INR1 crore.
Five to six vehicles to be 70-80% Make in India by 2027; components to be 100% indigenous in-house by this year or next financial year (per management).
Management said the company will move to quarterly reporting in the future, but not immediately; it is currently required to report half-yearly.
capex_capacity: Capacity expanded from 72,000 to 240,000 units per annum in FY26 across four plants.
Ladwa, Haryana flagship: 120,000 units per annum; serves North and West India.
Cuttack, Odisha: 60,000 units per annum, operational and GST-registered since December 2025; gateway to East and Northeast India.
Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu: about 60,000 units per annum, commissioned in July 2026 per the script (an answer said operational from next month); Tamil Nadu GST active.
Patan, Haryana: electric three-wheeler and two-wheeler chassis plant, commissioned in July 2026 per the script. Three-wheeler fabrication to be in-house after this plant starts.
Management said IPO proceeds funded plant and machinery, mainly for the three-wheeler segment; capital advances for new plant and machinery were about INR25 lakh.
demand_pricing: Management cited a low-speed EV segment of 8-10 lakh units per year (about 40-45% of EV two-wheeler volumes), growing 20-25% per annum, priced INR50,000-75,000 with no licence or registration needed.
Management said crude price increases and government encouragement are driving switching to EVs; expects market growth of 20-25%.
Management targets more than 10% share of the EV market this year and 20-30% within 2-3 years; an analyst's calculation implied roughly 10-11% share on 125,000 units against 11-12 lakh market.
Financing: management cited tie-ups with Bajaj, Kotak and Trusera Finance; said finance options are available in Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities.
Management said competition would not force price cuts; South India price list is expected to fall as Coimbatore transport costs decline.
Management said the monsoon has no effect on two-wheeler sales (IP67 motors and controllers); agricultural impact is said to delay, not reduce, sales.
Management expects 'no government support' for low-speed EVs currently beyond encouragement and registration/licence exemptions.

qa_highlights.question: Will a bad monsoon affect rural and Tier 2/3 demand, and how is consumer financing structured?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said monsoon does not hit sales (delays only) and cited tie-ups with Bajaj, Kotak and Trusera Finance for customer loans in Tier 1 and 2 cities.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of INR43 crore loans and advances on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Shubham Garg said supplier advances were about INR22.5 crore, capital advances INR25 lakh, and GST and customs refund claims INR19 crore, totalling about INR42.6 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate and how long does it last?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company has applied under Section 115BAB and pays 17% tax, which runs for 10 years from 2021, leaving about five years.

qa_highlights.question: How much will the Coimbatore plant produce and how does competition affect pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Coimbatore has about 60,000 units capacity, matching Odisha, and that lower transport costs will reduce South India prices without hurting EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin plans given higher branding spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it intends to keep profitability and margins similar while doubling or tripling volume, and that branding spend will not dent EBITDA or PAT growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is a bike segment planned, and how are three-wheeler service and spares handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no bike plans until battery costs fall; service engineers grew from four to more than 10, and the subsidiary handles spares.

risks_watch: Management's 75-80% growth and 125,000-unit targets rely on four plants and 550+ dealers being operational; the Coimbatore and Patan commissioning dates are stated in July 2026, after the period end.
Dependence on imported components (cells, from China and elsewhere) for parts not yet indigenised; management guided 70-80% Make in India by 2027.
Margin sustainability: management said EBITDA margin will hold despite higher promotion spend (IPL costs partly deferred as prepaid), and marketing spend for FY27 is undecided.
Three-wheeler volume was only 800 units in FY26, so the 2,000-unit FY27 target is an early-stage ramp.
Tax benefit under Section 115BAB runs about five more years; afterwards the tax rate is a risk.
Analyst concerns on the stock's periodic call auction; the company said it would write to SEBI and asked the broker to do the same.
Management did not explicitly break out segment-level profit or the subsidiary's contribution.
544563|2026-03.management_tone: Highly confident and promotional, with repeated claims of 'truth' and 'no losses'. Management was specific on volumes, plants and dealer counts, but answers on margins, subsidies, FY27 marketing budget and quarterly reporting were vague or deferred.
key_quotes: And I want every investor on this call to hear this clearly : not a single quarter of losses.
I am committed to sustaining 75% to 80% year-on-year revenue growth as our structural trajectory.
However much we expand, however much budget we keep, our focus is to keep profitability and margins similar.
We are targeting more than 125,000 units scale for this year.

rows.why: Three-wheeler in-house fabrication starts with Patan and the 2,000-unit target is new, but management said there are no bike plans until battery costs fall.

rows.why: Dealers to rise from more than 400 to more than 550 (100-150 new), with 100% of dealerships to be exclusive this year.

544567|2026-03.headline: Infinity Infoway FY26 revenue grew about 80% to INR 23.77 crore, with PAT up 60% to INR 7.01 crore, on ZeroTouch ramp-up.
544567|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue up about 80% to INR 23.77 crore, EBITDA up 64% to INR 10.57 crore and PAT up 60% to INR 7.01 crore, attributing growth to execution and operating leverage. The call centred on the patented ZeroTouch device-as-a-service product, with about 150 machines built and management guiding ZeroTouch to 20-22% of revenue in FY27. Other developments included a Gujarat government AI analytics order of about INR 10.97-11 crore, a TimePay prepaid card tie-up with NPST, and early Gulf (UAE) expansion. Figures were stated loosely on the call (for example "lakhs" used for crore), so the crore values should be verified against filings.

segments.commentary: About 53% of FY26 revenue; serves 55+ universities and 1,000+ schools and colleges, with more than 10 million students served to date.

segments.name: Industrial ERP
segments.commentary: About 36% of FY26 revenue; presence mainly in Gujarat, with Karnataka added during the year.

segments.name: Online examination system
segments.commentary: About 10% of FY26 revenue; concurrency of 2 lakh students and more than 25 lakh students examined online to date.

segments.name: ZeroTouch (device-as-a-service)
segments.commentary: Patented question-paper delivery system; around 150 machines ready, capacity of 3,000-4,000 machines in the short term, and management expects 20-22% of FY27 revenue from it at 50-60% margin.

segments.name: BrainZorg digital learning
segments.commentary: 10 courses hosted with 10,000+ students enrolled, free and paid; contributed 0.13% of FY26 revenue.

ZeroTouch machine innovation/launch planned for the current month, with meaningful ZeroTouch revenue expected within the quarter.
Intangible assets under development of about INR 8.15 crore, covering ZeroTouch software, an in-house LLM for ERP integration, and country-specific ERP adaptation for overseas expansion.
New sales teams deployed in eight Indian states; ZeroTouch also listed on GeM portal.
demand_pricing: Gujarat higher-education department AI-based data analytics order of about INR 10.97-11 crore; revenue expected to be recognised partly in FY27.
Annual university contract of about INR 1.45-1.5 crore from one MP institute.

Gulf/UAE expansion: team hired in the Gulf, selling through online demos and digital marketing; no material hurdles claimed despite regional war conditions. Saudi Arabia and Bahrain are next after UAE.
Management cites ZeroTouch addressable market of more than $3 billion a year in India, with DPDP law seen as a driver.
Competition from TCS ION and Zoho was raised; management says it has competed against larger players in 2-3 situations and focuses first on education, second on industry.
Turnkey project won (ERP plus smart classrooms, computers and servers) required purchase of hardware, which is why 'purchase of stock-in-trade' appeared as a new P&L line.

qa_highlights.question: Which international geographies are targeted and how will the Gulf war conditions be handled?
qa_highlights.answer: UAE is the first target, followed by Saudi Arabia and Bahrain. The company has hired a team in the Gulf and is selling through online demos and digital marketing, with no major hurdles so far.

qa_highlights.question: How does competitive risk from TCS ION and Zoho look for education and MSME ERP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it competed with larger players in 2-3 cases, focuses on education first, and has a presence in industry mainly in Gujarat plus Karnataka added this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ZeroTouch patent a process or product patent, and what are capacity and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a process patent covering question-paper generation through printing, stapling and packing. About 150 machines are ready, capacity is 3,000-4,000 in the short term, and expected margin is 50-60%.

qa_highlights.question: When will TimePay go live and how is revenue shared?
qa_highlights.answer: A pilot is complete and issuer approvals are pending for the NSDL payment bank card. Meaningful revenue is expected by quarter-end or early next quarter, on a transaction-based model shared with NPST and the issuer bank.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ZeroTouch market size and target share?
qa_highlights.answer: The Indian market is above $3 billion a year. The company currently has zero share and plans 1-2% this year and up to 10% later, through government tenders, GeM, private institutions and channel partners.

qa_highlights.question: What is in the INR 8.15 crore intangible assets under development and why is there a stock-in-trade purchase line?
qa_highlights.answer: Intangibles include ZeroTouch software, an in-house LLM for ERP and country-specific ERP development. Stock purchases relate to turnkey education projects that need hardware such as computers and servers.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 revenue growth and the ZeroTouch deployment ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 60-70% growth in FY27 and ZeroTouch at 20-22% of revenue. About 30% of the first 3,000 machines (around 900) are to be deployed next year, and a further 30-35% the year after.

544567|2026-06.headline: Infinity Infoway reported Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs. 689 lakhs, EBITDA Rs. 344 lakhs and PAT Rs. 201 lakhs, with ZeroTouch launched and Rs. 75 crore order book cited.

Sales and marketing headcount was expanded across multiple states, which drove higher employee cost. 544567|2026-09.headline: Infinity Infoway H1 FY27 revenue rose 106.22% to Rs 16.81 crore, with EBITDA margin at 50.68% and PAT margin at 29.89%.
544567|2026-09.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 (six months to 30 Sep 2026) revenue from operations of Rs 16.81 crore versus Rs 8.15 crore a year earlier, up 106.22%. EBITDA rose about 109.68% to Rs 8.52 crore (50.68% margin) and PAT rose 79.36% to Rs 5.02 crore (29.89% margin). Growth was supported by the ZeroTouch secured examination paper product, which began booking revenue in H1 with larger billing expected from Q3, and by a headcount increase from 156 to 178. Depreciation increased as products under development in FY26 went into use and as GPU and ZeroTouch device assets were added. Management also outlined plans to enter international markets, starting with the Gulf, then Southeast Asia and Europe.

segments.name: Education ERP (government and education clients)
segments.commentary: Serves 61+ education clients, with recurring revenue from 28; modules cover admissions, academics, examinations, finance, fees and HR (30+ modules). Management described it as the core business.

segments.name: Industry / enterprise ERP
segments.commentary: 35+ industry customers, with recurring revenue from 16; industrial ERP with AI-enabled solutions is a stated priority.

segments.name: ZeroTouch (secured examination paper solution)
segments.commentary: Early-stage revenue in H1 described as nominal; billing is per question paper printed and delivered, with exams started in October 2026 and a good amount of revenue expected in Q3. Management cites EBITDA margin above 50-60%, and 20-22% of revenue targeted from it within two years.

544570|2026-06.headline: WeWork India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28.5% YoY to INR698 crores and PAT reached INR53.2 crores (vs INR8.4 crores), with sequential dip from last quarter's customization one-off.
544570|2026-06.overview: Management asked investors to judge the quarter year-on-year, not sequentially, because Q4 FY26 included about INR47 crores of one-time customization income versus INR9.5 crores this quarter. Revenue grew 28.5% YoY to INR698 crores, company EBITDA rose 69% to INR138.3 crores at a 19.8% margin, and occupancy reached 84.9%. Capex was INR188 crores in the quarter, FCFF was negative INR46 crores, and net debt fell to INR31.6 crores. Management reaffirmed FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth above 20% and capex guidance of INR500-600 crores, and it changed the accounting treatment for large managed-office customization.

from 10.4%; credit rating moved from A- to A+

qa_highlights.question: Will there be one-time customization revenue from the 15,000-16,000 seats opening this quarter, and how fast do new seats reach EBITDA break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 20,000 seats open by October and all cohorts are already profitable. Customization will be recognised over the contract term for large managed-office work, with a run-rate of INR10-15 crores a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR500-600 crore capex guidance being kept?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, guidance is held; any change depends on large managed-office deals, with visibility by the next quarter.

qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect a dip. Margin is seen moving up because about 7,000 managed-office seats open in Q2, and management points to a 19-20% margin range.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20%+ growth guidance intact on a quarterly basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth above 20%, citing about 70% YoY EBITDA growth; it expects EBITDA to rise each quarter from the Rs138 crore base.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the decline in mature and growth-cohort occupancy and the seat exits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mature-cohort capacity rose about 8,000 seats as a result of cohort migration. Growth-cohort occupancy fell from 73% to 65% because about 7,000 new seats opened, and mature-cohort EBITDA margin is holding at about 28%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the managed-office customization model work and could REITs compete?
qa_highlights.answer: Customization is billed upfront when clients ask for changes beyond the contract price and is now amortised over the term. Management argues clients prefer one operator across formats, and REITs typically require longer commitments.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Rivet and Member Services economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Rivet is a 10-15% margin business with direct flow-through to PAT and no capex. Member Services take rates are 6-16% plus listing fees, and some services will be booked as margin rather than revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the promoter share pledge?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% of shares are pledged against roughly INR570 crores of residual debt; about 30 lakh shares release next quarter, and the goal is to clear the pledge in FY27 via asset sales or a block deal.

key_quotes: Look at us on a year-over-year basis, not sequentially, for two reasons.

This is not a warning sign, it is a model working as it is designed.

So, this will now from this year onwards actually smoothen out any type of lumpiness that we basically saw last year, and you'll have a more recurring base of customization revenue as the quarter's kind of flow through.
We don't foresee the margin dipping; we actually see potentially the margin moving upwards because of the large managed offices that are a component of that expansion coming up in Q2.

544570|2026-09.headline: WeWork India Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31.6% YoY to INR768.7 crore and EBITDA margin reached 21.2%, with PAT up 67.4% to INR65.8 crore.
544570|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was a strong quarter: revenue grew 31.6% YoY and 10.1% QoQ to about INR768.7 crore, and EBITDA rose 37.6% YoY to INR162.9 crore at a 21.2% margin. The company added a record ~11,700 desks in the quarter, taking capacity to 145,300 desks across 85 centres, while occupancy rose 357 bps YoY to 83.7%. Net debt of INR310 crore a year ago turned into net cash of INR23 crore, and ROCE reached 34.5%. Management guided to 150,000-155,000 desks by March 2027, and the company is laying out a 190,000-200,000 seat path. All figures are on an IGAAP-equivalent basis.

segments.name: Core flex / membership
segments.commentary: Core business revenue INR657.7 crore, up 31.7% YoY. Members grew 32.5% to about 121,700, and occupancy reached 83.7% (mature centres ~88%, growth centres 64.8% vs 51.4% a year ago).

segments.name: Value-added services (VAS)
segments.commentary: VAS revenue INR79.6 crore, up 35% YoY; management says VAS is margin accretive. Customization revenue about INR18 crore in Q2 and about INR30 crore in H1, with flow-through to EBITDA.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Digital revenue INR29.2 crore, up 46% YoY, operating at close to 80% EBITDA margin.

guidance_outlook: Desk count expected at about 150,000-155,000 by March 2027 (145,300 at Sept 30; ~4,500 added by Oct 5, so already ~150,000); some March deliveries could slip to early April.
Longer term: path to about 190,000-200,000 seats, with FY28 and FY29 supply under negotiation; management says FY28 rollout will be higher than FY27.
Margins: Q3 and Q4 to see further expansion as occupancy rises, with larger step-up in Q4 as rent freezes expire; capacity additions lower in the next two quarters.
FY27 capex about INR500-odd crore for the full year (H2 lower than H1's INR363.8 crore, though one large deal adds capex). FY28 capex likely near INR600 crore or slightly more.
FCFO-to-EBITDA conversion expected in a 1.2x-1.5x range.
PAT margin hovering in 7%-10% range going forward; EBITDA margin range of 20%-23% for next year, depending on capacity timing.
Largest-ever deal to be announced next quarter; expected to require significant capex on a single asset.
capex_capacity: Desks at 145,300 across 85 centres in 8 cities (+27% YoY); ~11,700 desks added in Q2 (record), ~18,400 in H1, ~4,500 more in October.
Bengaluru 54,000 desks (anchor); Hyderabad 20,000 (now second-largest, overtook Mumbai); Pune 17,000.
Q2 additions: Chennai ~3,600 desks (managed office extension), Hyderabad ~2,700 (WeWork-branded), Pune ~2,600 (managed offices).

Pipeline: 9,000+ desks under signed leases and fit-out, ~38,000 seats under LOI; total ~47,000 incremental seats (32% above current capacity). Management cites a further ~2 million sq ft of prospective space not yet at LOI stage.
Growth centres (open <12 months) hold ~25,000 desks; portfolio breakeven occupancy 55.7%. Refurbishment cycles expected around year 5-7 per asset.
demand_pricing: Revenue-to-rent multiple at an all-time high of 2.7x; new large managed-office deals are at about 3x, driven by higher capex per sq ft.
Contracted escalations of 6%-7% on existing contracts; renewal rate about 80%-85% in H1 FY27; churn lower than expected.
Average commitment term rose to about 28 months (larger accounts ~32 months).
Locked-in core revenue grew ~66% to INR3,843 crore against INR1,421 crore of rent, about 2.7x coverage (management also cites ~2.9x in Q&A).
Enterprises 77% of core revenue; GCCs ~41% of mix; other global companies ~26%; Fortune 500 ~30%; top 10 members 23% of revenue.
Minimum wage increases in Karnataka near 60% and backdated BESCOM energy tariffs pressured opex per sq ft in H1; management says margin would be ~22%-23% without these.

qa_highlights.question: How has underwriting changed for new centres (payback, revenue-to-rent) given rising competition and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is taking larger positions in Grade A assets, underwriting buildings under development, and doing multi-property deals; it says underwriting is smarter but not drastically changed versus two years ago. Payback periods are improving and capex control is driving better returns.

qa_highlights.question: Renewal trends and pricing on renewals versus new contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewal rate 80%-85% in H1; renewal escalations are lower than contracted escalations and pricing on fill-up, as management trades price for loyalty and scale. Around 50% of customer growth comes from existing members expanding.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation between expansion and FCF, and use of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: More FY28 expansion is planned with additional capex; the company is also looking at buybacks or dividends once book losses are cleared, and at investing in adjacent businesses that help Indian companies scale.

qa_highlights.question: Customization revenue in Q2 and EBITDA flow-through; GCC hiring outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Customization was about INR18 crore in Q2 and about INR30 crore in H1, with flow-through to EBITDA; management says large lumpiness is normalised. Management sees GCCs continuing to set up in India and expects demand to grow, with premium managed offices and more amenities.

qa_highlights.question: Will March 2027 desk target of 155,000 be met, and what H2 margin uplift to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Already at about 150,000 desks; 155,000 visibility by March, though some deliveries may slip into early April. Margins to expand further in Q3 and Q4, with the larger step-up in Q4 as rent freezes expire. Q4 YoY margin change expected to be modest given a strong Q4 last year.

qa_highlights.question: Margin guidance for next year and pipeline beyond FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No precise percentage guidance; FY28 EBITDA margin range of 20%-23%, depending on capacity timing. Pipeline: about 2 million sq ft of additional prospective space not yet signed; leases signed about 12 months out with ~95% visibility, 70%-80% at 18-24 months.

risks_watch: Opex inflation: Karnataka minimum wage hikes near 60% and BESCOM backdated energy tariffs; margin outlook depends on it.
Depreciation rising with the largest capex cycle; PAT margin guided at 7%-10%.
Commonwealth Bank of Australia (~1.2 million sq ft built-to-suit campus in Manyata, a customer for ~7 years) is expected to move out; timing uncertain. Another possible lumpy move-out next year.
Promoter pledge still outstanding; management says it will reduce it over time, with no block sale at current prices, and has three years to repay the debt.
Capex upside risk if more managed-office deals are signed; one very large deal to be announced next quarter.
Desk target of 155,000 by March 2027 could slip into early April.

We are in no hurry to close it, because we have three years to basically sort of like pay that debt off, and clearly the business is growing faster than the cost of capital that we have for that debt.
So, capex would possibly be closer to the INR600 crores mark, or maybe even slightly more than that for FY28.

544572|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 sales rose 9.8% QoQ to INR 9.5 billion; reported PBT margin 9.5%, or 11.5% excluding demerger one-offs.
544572|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 (Jan–Mar 2026) revenue grew 9.8% QoQ to INR 9.5 billion, led by OEM orders from wind, metals and rail. Reported PBT margin recovered to 9.5% from negative 7.8% in Q3, but this includes demerger-related one-offs; excluding them, margin was 11.5% versus 13.1% in Q3. Net working capital fell 2.8% QoQ to 18.7% of sales on lower inventory. Management guided margins back to around 13% after demerger costs end and about 15% by FY29-30, with capex of around INR 800 crore planned through FY30 for a new Pune plant. YoY comparisons were not presented because prior-period figures were extracted from SKF India Limited.

from -7.8% in Q3 FY26; +1,731 bps QoQ

segments.commentary: Distribution fell in Q4, with share dropping to 32% from 38%, as volume shifted away from distributors with overdue payments and some shipments were held back. Management expects this to recover.

segments.commentary: Exports performed well in Q4, mainly to Europe and Southeast Asia; about 6% of FY26 revenue.

segments.commentary: Intercompany sales to SKF India Limited were the second-largest growth driver in Q4, linked to automotive demand; about 4% of FY26 revenue.

guidance_outlook: Margin (excl. one-offs) expected to return to around 13% by end of calendar 2026 as demerger costs finish and distribution mix recovers.
Long-term target of about 15% PBT margin by FY29-30, with 16-18% as aspiration but not committed.
Net working capital expected at 19-20% of sales going forward.
Growth expected around 8% in the interim until the new Pune plant is operational.
Expect to pass on FX impact and 3-4% cost escalation through price increases; pricing actions already taken with distributors.
capex_capacity: Total capex of around INR 800 crore plus over FY26 to FY30, mainly for the new Pune plant and new DGBB and TRB channels.
New Pune plant expected to start operating mid-2028, with full channel transfer and ramp-up complete by end of calendar 2028.
Tapered roller bearing capacity at Pune raised from 600,000 to 886,000 pieces via machine upgrades; cost down about 18%, changeover time down 20%, new product lead time down about 35%.
Until the new plant is ready, SKF India Limited continues job-work manufacturing; additional demand sourced from SKF Ahmedabad and Nilai.
demand_pricing: Industrial production grew about 4.5% YoY; construction grew 6.6% and iron and steel production 9.7%.
Wind is primarily India-driven; India is described as the fastest-growing wind market. Company exited wind and some rail (freight) and tractor business earlier and is re-entering due to localization.
Q4 margin was pressured by OEM mix (lower margin) and higher employee cost from full 100% bonus accrual versus partial payout in Q3.

Other expenses rose on royalty and trademark payments (about INR 60 million higher) and manufacturing costs (repairs, power and fuel, stores). A transfer pricing margin on services from SKF India was also booked.
Competition described as intense, especially at OEMs. Rupee depreciation is a bigger cost headwind than steel and oil-linked inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 segment-wise mix across general machinery, heavy industries, metals, railway, wind, OEM, aftermarket and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26: distribution about 35%, OEM about 51%, exports about 6%, SKF India sales about 4%, other income about 3%. Within OEM: railway 11%, general machinery 7%, wind and defence 7%, heavy industries 7%, metals 6%.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw material inflation trending, how much price has been taken, and how will margins evolve with capacity additions and demerger costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin to return to about 13% by end of calendar 2026; about 15% by FY29-30. Cost escalation projected at 3-4%, with FX as the bigger headwind. Pricing actions already taken with distributors; OEM price escalation being negotiated and expected to be harder.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gap between current margins and the 13-15% historical range, and what drives the path to 16-18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Drags are extra investments in Pune including the new plant, intense OEM competition, higher railway mix, and higher depreciation. Management targets around 15% through 2030 and says 16-18% is an aspiration that cannot yet be committed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company prioritise growth over margin, given exits and re-entries in wind, rail and tractors?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy is growth while maintaining margin, with a target of about 15%. Re-entering wind, freight rail and tractor segments through localization means winning share at lower OEM margins, which management expects to improve through efficiency and pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex timeline and when will new capacity be commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of around INR 800 crore plus over FY26 to FY30. New Pune plant expected to be operational mid-2028, with full ramp-up and channel transfers complete by end of 2028.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 350-400 crore channel expansion investment and how will growth be delivered until the new plant is ready?
qa_highlights.answer: The investment is plant and machinery for DGBB and TRB channels at the new Pune plant, not warehouses. Growth is guided at about 8% in the interim, supported by job-work from SKF India and sourcing from Ahmedabad and Nilai.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the demerger cost roll-off, distribution mix recovery, and price pass-through of FX and 3-4% cost escalation, especially with OEM customers.
Rupee depreciation and steel and oil-linked costs could widen the cost gap.
Heavy intercompany activity with SKF India Limited: sales, transfer pricing margin, royalty and payables/receivables settlement could affect working capital.

544572|2026-06.headline: SKF India (Industrial) Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.3% YoY to INR 9,708 mn, but PBT margin fell to ~9% on FX losses and demerger IT costs.
544572|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 9,708 million, up 18.3% YoY (on management's constructed comparison) and 2.6% QoQ. PBT was INR 869 million, a margin of about 9%, hit by roughly INR 147 million of forex loss and about INR 150 million of demerger-related IT separation cost. Operating cash conversion was 63%, with a one-time outflow for name change and land transfer. Management reiterated a long-term PBT margin path of 14-16% through 2028, with a 17-19% aspiration, and a new Pune plant with INR 850-950 crore capex targeted for 2028.

financial_highlights.change: Down QoQ due to forex and demerger one-offs
Rupee depreciation, linked to Middle East war; on imports mainly from Europe
Incremental one-time cost in the quarter
Operating cash flow hit by name-change and land-transfer charges

segments.name: General machinery (pumps, motors, gears)
segments.commentary: Management called general machinery the strongest segment this quarter and said its share of business has grown.

segments.name: Wind and heavy industry
segments.commentary: Named as other strong performers in the quarter; rail described as solid.

segments.name: Distribution channel
segments.commentary: Highest-margin channel; management cited high double-digit margins versus high single-digit for OE.

segments.name: OE channel
segments.commentary: About 54% of revenue; lower margin but supports aftermarket share growth.

segments.name: Solutions (services, remanufacturing, condition monitoring)
segments.commentary: Around 6-7% of India business, below 10%; being scaled with added technology and direct sales staff.

guidance_outlook: Long-term PBT margin guidance of 14-16%, described as conservative; aspiration 17-19%, with near-term pressure from investments through 2028.
Management expects demerger IT costs to continue for two more quarters, tapering by end-2026 and ceasing around Q4/Q1 FY28.
Management said ~12% is a fair margin on current performance excluding the one-offs; manufacturing efficiency could add a couple of percentage points more.
Aspiration to double the India Industrial business in about five years, with no firm timeline committed.
Pune plant (capex INR 850-950 crore; 900-950 in one remark) expected to start production in 2028, with payback of 5-7 years including channel transfers and new third-party and SKF group channels.
Sujeeth Pai to succeed Mukund Vasudevan as MD effective 1 September 2026.
capex_capacity: New Pune factory is the key constraint: majority of new channel installations are tied to the factory coming online in 2028; capacity is currently constrained by space, not demand.
New tapered roller bearing (TRB) line in Pune adds 3 million units annually, serving agriculture, gearbox and aftermarket; supports exports too.
One additional TRB channel to be added by early 2027 despite capacity constraints.
Plan to add around 15-20 lines, some transferred from SKF group companies and some new; most depend on the new factory.
Capex plan quoted as INR 900-950 crore in prepared remarks and INR 850-900 crore in later Q&A; figures are inconsistent in the transcript.
demand_pricing: Order book reported as growing, with sustained growth over the last few quarters.
INR 140 crore gearbox-manufacturer order (wind-related, one-year, spread through the year) and INR 35 crore agricultural tractor OEM contract.
Innovation traction strongest in general machinery (gearboxes, motors, pumps); agriculture uses customised offerings.
Data center and humanoid opportunities are early-stage; current data center traction is in basic pumps, with no material revenue yet.
Management said the Indian Automotive sales share is being reduced to improve mix.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the margin moderation from the 16-19% guidance to 14-16%, and how much is FX and demerger impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 14-16% is the conservative long-term path and 17-19% the aspiration; near-term margins dip due to investments. CFO quantified FX plus demerger one-offs at about 3% of margin, implying ~12% underlying.

qa_highlights.question: What is the supply and recurrence profile of the INR 140 crore wind and INR 35 crore agri orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Most orders are one-time or one-year contracts, typically extending one to two years. Some services and condition-monitoring contracts are longer-term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin difference across distribution, OE and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution is the higher-margin channel at high double-digit margins; OE is high single-digit. OE supports aftermarket share growth.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the solutions business and what is the doubling timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Solutions are around 6-7% of India business, below 10% in aspiration. Doubling the business is an aspiration within five years at the outside, with no committed timeline.

qa_highlights.question: When will one-off costs end, and is 12% margin achievable now?
qa_highlights.answer: The IT cost should taper through end-2026 and stop around Q4 FY27/Q1 FY28. CFO said ~12% is a fair current margin, with further gains from efficiency and the Pune plant.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company merge with the SKF automotive or other group entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no active plans; it wants the demerger to stabilise first but continuously evaluates options.

risks_watch: Forex: rupee depreciation linked to Middle East tensions raised import costs on European-sourced products; margin impact depends on INR movement.

Motor Finance turned profitable at INR43 crore PAT in Q4 after breaking even in Q3, though its AUM fell 4% QoQ to INR25,390 crore. qa_highlights.question: Impact of the West Asia conflict on clients and segments?

qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to analytics-led underwriting, GenAI-based model building and conservative credit policy together; quarterly consolidated credit cost fell from 1.6% in Q1 to 0.9% in Q4 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Will the CV book keep growing given the cycle?

qa_highlights.question: Expected NIM and spread trajectory in FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY28 ROA target achievable and what are the levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers are cost-to-income reduction via technology and AI, branch productivity from adding products per branch, and scale benefits; management said credit cost of about 1% and opex savings of about 15bp, with NIM plus fee making up the rest.

qa_highlights.question: Is the stress in April visible in PL/BL and in the SME book?

544574|2026-06.headline: Tata Capital Q1 FY27 PAT rose 56% YoY to INR1,547 crore, with consolidated AUM up 22% YoY to INR2.91 lakh crore and credit cost at 1%.
544574|2026-06.overview: Consolidated PAT of INR1,547 crore grew 56% YoY and 3% QoQ, with ROA at 2.3% (2.5% ex-Motor Finance) and ROE at 13.7%. AUM reached INR2.91 lakh crore, up 22% YoY and 5% QoQ, or 28% YoY excluding Motor Finance. Disbursements rose 33% YoY to INR46,212 crore, while the book grew about 10% YoY on a legacy run-off drag. segments.name: Housing Finance (Tata Capital Housing Finance)

segments.name: Motor Finance
segments.commentary: Book moderated to INR24,445 crore as of June 2026 after a sequential decline; legacy net AUM run-off reduced to INR945 crore from INR3,139 crore a year earlier. Business remained profitable in Q1 FY27 despite seasonal credit cost rise.

segments.name: Unsecured Retail
segments.commentary: Unsecured retail disbursements up 50% YoY; unsecured retail AUM up 17% YoY. Management says the unsecured book will grow faster than overall book in FY27.

segments.commentary: Retail plus SME is 85.4% of the portfolio, within the 85-88% target band; Corporate is the balance. Management says Corporate has 'maxed out' and will be syndicated down if originated above target.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan strategy and state expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Approval expected by year-end; about 500+ branches over 2.5-3 years and INR4,000-5,000 crore portfolio; target states identified but not disclosed, with some in northern India. Acquired entity to be renamed under Tata Capital once a subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: Monsoon and El Nino impact on rural and vehicle books?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has seen no impact on the portfolio so far and sees no early signs of stress.

risks_watch: Cost of funds rising on incremental borrowing (7.28% vs 7.15% QoQ); management guides +8-10 bps for FY27.
Motor Finance book shrinking QoQ; turnaround to growth expected from Q3 FY27 and ROA target of 2% by FY28.
Rising unsecured book and new gold loan segment; approvals from RBI for Yogloans pending until about year-end.
Macro risks flagged: elevated energy prices, El Nino/monsoon, CPI at 4.38% in June, and possible repo rate hike (management is rate-neutral in guidance).
Credit cost held at about 1% despite new products; Q1 benefited from seasonal benign trend, and management noted that the Q1 credit cost was 'in line with FY28 guidance'.
PCR movements (30-40 bps QoQ) tied to Stage-3 ageing; monitor provisioning trend.
544574|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Q1 growth, asset quality and operating leverage, with the CEO calling it an 'excellent quarter'. Cautious on macro risks such as energy prices, El Nino and funding costs, and conservative on CV, construction equipment and petro-reliant MSME segments. Evasive on specific gold-loan target states and the timing of Housing Finance listing.
key_quotes: Our asset quality metrics remains resilient, underscoring the strength of our portfolio, underwriting discipline and collections infrastructure.
we expect the gap to narrow over the next 2-3 quarters as sustained origination momentum translates into book expansion.
whatever comes further from credit cost will be a bonus. We are not factoring that in.
we are fairly, I would say, optimistic on meeting our guidance which we have given to the market.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides NIM up about 10 bps over FY27 and FY28 ROA to 2.6% from 2.3%, with two-thirds from margin expansion; high-margin products are 38% of disbursements and incremental lending is being repriced, though cost of funds rises 8-10 bps and cost-to-income is 36.4%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 onward (gold loans 500+ branches over 2.5-3 years po
rows.why: Yogloans acquisition (162 branches, about INR708 crore AUM as of March 2026) targets 500+ branches and INR4,000-5,000 crore portfolio over 2.5-3 years, but it is subject to RBI approval expected by calendar year-end; only 14 branches were added organically in Q1 on a 1,491-branch network.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Disbursements up 33% YoY to INR46,212 crore and consolidated AUM up 22% YoY (28% ex-Motor Finance), with FY27 AUM growth guided at 23-25% and management saying it is on track; book growth expected to converge toward disbursement growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management has no capex guidance; capex is a small INR93 crore primary infusion into Yogloans, and utilisation is not disclosed, so a new capex announcement is only conditional on gold-loan expansion and the RBI approval.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says credit cost improvement beyond 1% is upside and FY28 ROA 2.6% and cost-to-income 33-34% are on track, but FY27 guidance is only reiterated and the Q1 credit cost benefited from a seasonal benign trend.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cost of funds rose to 7.28% from 7.15% QoQ with guidance for a further 8-10 bps rise in FY27, and management flagged macro risks (energy prices, El Nino, CPI 4.38%, possible repo hike) and Stage-3 PCR rising 30-40 bps QoQ.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management expects high-yield product contribution to rise by Q3 or Q4 FY27, unsecured retail disbursements are up 50% YoY, and Micro Housing (about INR1,200 crore) is planned to grow about 100% in FY27.

rows.label: Yogloans gold loans entry (500+ branches, INR4,000-5,000 crore AUM in 2.5-3 year
rows.when: approval by calendar year-end, then 2.5-3 years
rows.why: Acquisition of about 88.6% stake for up to INR318 crore pre-money equity valuation, with 162 branches and AUM about INR708 crore as of March 2026, pending RBI approval.

rows.label: Incremental repricing to protect margins
rows.why: Management is repricing incremental lending across Housing, Retail, SME and Corporate, with no PLR hikes taken so far, and yields raised in each Motor Finance segment.
